Market: My listings is split into the List form, your listings, auctions, bids and buy orders, form fields are labelled (a stall's "Put up a piece" form too), and the List button is full size again
Market: the Vendors list has the same column names
Notice Board: the window now downloads in the background after the game starts, so it is usually ready the first time it is opened
Market: starts loading as soon as the board opens
Seat Tab: loads its standings and works at the same time
Seat Tab: the guild war is split into panels: the Charter, This week (Muster, Reckoning, Turning), the battle, Standings, Your guild, the holder's orders, the Works and the Chronicle
Seat Tab: each challenging guild has a bar showing how close it is to claiming the Charter or winning the Right of Siege
Seat Tab: a new "How the seat war works" guide covers pledging, earning influence, claiming, sieges and holding
Notice Board: messages across the board, Market, Work, Vendors and Seat tabs are shorter and plainer, for example "The market did not load."

Word Filter: slurs and crude words are starred out in chat on every channel, Notice Board notes, guild notes, letters and shared journal pages, leaving the rest of the message and ordinary words that merely contain one alone
Word Filter: notes pinned before the update are starred too when a board is read
Word Filter: a guild rank name or a ship's name with such a word is refused, and the message names the word
Word Filter: a custom class name with such a word is not shown to other players, and a maker's mark with one is left off the item
Word Filter: a name given with the Item Maker is starred wherever the item is shown
Profile: the inspect card is tidied: the name always keeps its line, badges sit on their own row under it, and the duel, breach, town and serpent records are compact plaques
Profile: worn gear is grouped into In hand, Armour, Clothing and Jewellery, with a pair such as two rings sharing one row
Wallet: the sheet is now a ledger: Coin (gold, silver) and In the wallet (letters of credit, Deadlands Embers, Welkynd Shards), with each amount lined up on the right
Enhanced Lighting: the shadow cache is on again by default, so lamp-lit rooms such as taverns, shops and guild halls get their frame rate back

Enhanced Lighting: shadows no longer flicker on Windows, a rapid strobing on some NVIDIA cards and every shadow in a room blinking at once on others, caused by how cached shadows were copied on Direct3D
Enhanced Lighting: the "Shadow cache (faster, may flicker)" switch is gone, as it is no longer needed
Off-Road Placement: trees, bushes and rocks no longer stand on roads and tracks and their branches no longer hang over them, including the 3D trees from Low Poly Trees
Off-Road Placement: herb patches, ore veins on open stone and Motherlodes keep off the roads too
Off-Road Placement: forests no longer grow across dirt tracks
Off-Road Placement: the Clear roadsides setting is on by default; off lets them grow up to the road edge, as Daggerfall does

Blended Climates: where two climates meet the border wanders and breaks into patches about two hundred metres deep instead of a straight line: grass thins into sand, rock creeps into the woods, snow comes in drifts
Blended Climates: trees follow the same border, each tree near it belonging to the climate of the ground it stands on
Grass: follows the blended climate border too

Blended Climates: the Blended climates setting is on by default; off changes climates at a straight edge, as Daggerfall does; it takes effect on the next world load and is always on online so everyone sees the same trees
Cover: in winter, the trees of a wood are cover the way they are the rest of the year: enemies hide behind the trunk and under the crown
Townspeople: big cities no longer drop to a frame or two a second between 4 and 6 in the morning (game time).
Harbours: a port whose harbour lies far from any street no longer searches for its dock four times a second.
Repairs: Repairs Objects now mends the gear you are wearing.
Repairs: weapons mend at a dagger's pace.
Meditation Candle: it no longer refills what a smith won't repair.
Magic Repair: armour, clothing and jewellery still mend Daggerfall's 1 point at a time.
Magic Repair: enchanted items still mend only with Allow Magic Repairs, which is on by default and always on online.
Magic Repair: it still mends one piece every four game minutes, and only for you
Grass: the grass grows by default again, at Full, in the meadow style.
Grass: if you picked Half, Quarter or Off yourself, your choice is kept.
Grass: the grass is cheaper to draw, and looks exactly the same.
Grass: if the outdoors still run slow, Features > Grass > Half halves the grass's cost.

Yard: lamp posts, torches, braziers and the other lights you place in your home's yard now light the ground and walls around them at night, the way the town's street lamps light theirs: the same light (a warm flame with Enhanced Lighting, white without it) and the same flicker, from 17:00 to 08:00, the hours the town's lanterns are lit.
Yard: up to eight lamps light in each yard, the most any Daggerfall town block has.
Yard: a lamp you scale up casts a bigger pool of light.
Yard: lamps you placed before this update light up on their own.
Professions: mining, Logging, Herbalism (the Basket included), Fishing and Hunting no longer stop for the day.
Gathering Nodes: each node can still be worked once a day by each character, so the next harvest is wherever the next node stands.
Professions: the chip under the compass shows the day's count without a limit ("Mining 34 - 12 today"), and so does the Professions tab.
Accounts: rare hides (tiers 5 and 6): 3 a day for your account.
Accounts: veins in dungeons nobody has vouched for: 4 a day for your account.
Castle Daggerfall: the two towers in Castle Daggerfall's courtyard are whole again.
Project Legacy: Project Legacy: the Family tab's House page can now move your family's seat to the town you are standing in.
Project Legacy: your heirs are born in the new seat, your fallen can be laid to rest there, and a family without a home of its own lives there.
Project Legacy: when you aren't standing in another town, the House page tells you how to move the seat.
Privateer's Hold: online, every character now starts Privateer's Hold on their own, with its enemies alive, its doors shut and its loot untouched.
Dungeons: if you step out and come back in the same session, the enemies you defeated and the chests you emptied stay that way for up to an hour, as in other dungeons online.
Privateer's Hold: local chat in the Hold now tells you that nobody can hear you there.
Climbing: you can no longer climb while you fast travel on the Overworld, whether on a journey or holding the movement keys under the travel view.
Climbing: you can't start a journey while hanging on a wall.
Climbing: Climbing works as before at walking pace.
Banishment: WAITS: four long online waits shortened - bank hours, Daedra summoning, the King of Worms' messenger, banishment
Textures: the steel plate cuirass now has its skirt, painted with its own texture.
Morrowind Body: the steel plate no longer T-poses in game.
Morrowind Body: attacks now keep up with your attack speed.
Morrowind Body: other players' fast attacks play at their pace too.
Morrowind Body: casting a spell plays the Morrowind casting animation through to the end, and the spell leaves your hands on the cast's release.
Weapons: your weapon leaves your hand while a spell is readied.

Area Spells: with Morrowind data installed, spells use Morrowind's own effects: the glow around the caster and on your hands, the bolt a target spell flies as, the hit on whoever it lands on, and the burst of an area spell.
Features: new switch under Features > Combat: Morrowind Spell Effects, on by default.
Travel Options: with Travel Options on, a journey down a steep road follows the road instead of flying off it into a fall.
Travel Options: if the roads arrive after you have loaded in (online, or on a slow connection), whatever lies on the ground stays on it as the ground settles, and so do you.
Loot Rarity: resistance from rolled gear now counts up to 45% per element, and only fills an Aetheric piece's resistance up to that same 45%.
Loot Drops: luck now multiplies drop chances (half at Luck 0, half again at Luck 100) instead of adding a flat amount.

Loot Rarity: clothing can drop as Magic and Rare with lines of its own: standing with a social group, warmth and weatherproofing (for Climates & Calories), Personality, and street skills - footwear leans to movement skills.
Loot Rarity: superior and Masterwork clothing you make now comes out Magic and Rare, as crafted weapons and armour already did.

Loot Rarity: six Legendary garments, each with a power: the Alik'r Wayfarer's Robes (the heat is felt 20 less), the Wrothgar Pass Mantle (the cold is felt 20 less), the Vestments of Stendarr (Restoration spells cost 25% less), the Pilgrim's Sandals (you tire 25% slower, falls hurt half as much), the Silks of Queen Barenziah (+5 standing with every group) and the Shade's Cowl (+25 Stealth while hooded).
Loot Rarity: with the loot rarity setting off, clothing stays exactly as in Daggerfall.

Loot Rarity: one Rare or Legendary in twelve from a body or a pile is cursed: one extra bonus line and one drawback (a bad reputation, bad reactions, damage or wear in holy places, weaker blows against a kind of foe, or a health leech).
Temples: a temple's Cure Disease priest now offers Lift Curse: the drawback goes, the bonus line stays.
Loot Rarity: hone: raise one line within its own range.
Welkynd Shards: scry: name a kind of foe and the guild marks the nearest dungeon of theirs in your region that isn't on your map yet (3 Welkynd Shards and 500 gold).
Loot Rarity: sockets: some Rares and Legendaries carry an empty socket.
Salvage: Salvage every Magic: one button on the Salvage page, asked first.
Inventory: item cards now compare what the item would change against what it would replace: up or down by how much, "new", and the lines you would lose.
Inventory: junk: mark gear as junk from its card, and "Sell junk" at a shop puts every junk piece on the counter in one press.
Inventory: quick loot has a new "Take gear" setting (All, Magic+, Rare+) for the take-all key.
Restore: the Welkynd Stone (fills your magicka) and the Varla Stone (restores every enchanted item you wear, magic items' charges included) can turn up in the deepest places.
Notice Board: towns have all their Notice Boards again.
Hoods: a raised hood now shields a vampire from the sun.
Pirates: the Carrack (the pirate flagship and the merchant carrack) is a new model, fully textured.
Ships: the carrack has ten gunports, each with its own shutter, and a gun on a platform behind every port
Companions: a companion through her middle house leads down to her gun deck.
Ships: the carrack's wheel and rudder turn together
Lantern: she carries seven lanterns, so a carrack at sea is lit at night.
Ships: the carrack's rig is a spritsail, fore and main courses, a main topsail and a lateen mizzen
Pirates: the Large Boat (the pirate sloop and the coasting trader) is a new clinker-built model.
Ships: all seven of the large boat's sail plans are rebuilt on the new hull
Ships: the large boat steers by a tiller, a raked rudder on its sternpost with the helmsman on a step at its stern
Ships: seven swivel guns sit on the large boat's gunwale, three a side and one at its bow
Ship Strength: a carrack's broadside still hits as hard as before, now from five guns a side instead of seven.
Pirates: the pirate sloop now closes to 50 m (it was 55), because the new boat is a taller target.
Revenants: a beaten revenant of rank 1 or 2 now usually breaks and runs, and it really gets away.
Revenants: a fleeing foe now sprints at twice its walk, which is faster than a player running at average Speed and Running.
Revenants: fixed: a foe that broke while circling you used to keep circling instead of running away.
Revenants: from rank 3 nothing changes: you still break its will to make it kneel.
Low Poly Trees: Low Poly trees no longer hang over roads, tracks or town streets.
Low Poly Trees: Trees still stand exactly where they did.
Low Poly Trees: this follows the Clear roadsides option, which is on by default.
Hoods: a raised hood now protects a character whose class has the Damage from Sunlight disadvantage.
Hoods: bare-headed, the sun works as before.
Hoods: a hood carried in your pack, not worn, doesn't count.
Eye of the Beholder: your third-person sprite no longer flickers between two directions when you start running or strafing at an angle.
Eye of the Beholder: an attack now plays one swing instead of a swing and a follow-through.
Eye of the Beholder: the "PingPong Offset" setting no longer does anything.
Revenants: a revenant you beat with a party now always kneels for your judgement (or makes its last stand first).
Invisibility: you can now interact with your party members while they are under Chameleon, Shadow or Invisibility, and they can interact with you.
Invisibility: concealed players outside your party stay hidden from all of these, as before.
Enhanced Combat Visuals: how concealed players are drawn has not changed.
Titles: players who first played on the evening of September 24 in the Americas now hold the Founder title.
Titles: played before September 25 on another device or browser?
Morrowind Models: shift-click an item in your pack to drop it in front of you as itself.
Morrowind Models: each item shows its own picture: its Morrowind model when Morrowind data is attached, its classic picture otherwise.
Morrowind Models: rarity shows on the ground: Magic-or-better items get an outline in their tier's colour, and Rare-or-better ones stand the same line of light the world boss's spoils do.
Morrowind Models: items come to rest against walls rather than through them, stop moving while the game is paused, and ride along with a body on a moving deck.
Morrowind Models: settings are under Features > Physical Items by demifiend000: turn it off, choose which kinds of loot spill from bodies, how hard it is thrown, and how big items are.
Profile: the profile that opens from your portrait in the top-right corner has been reorganised.

Profile: underneath, it is split into sections: Record (duels, breaches closed, towns defended, serpents slain, silver, each in its own tile, with a bar for the share of duels you've won), Characters (each character's Renown, with a bar showing progress to the next level), Wardrobe and Account.
Profile: on a wide screen the sections sit side by side in two columns.
Profile: the Close, Sign out and Change password buttons stay pinned to the bottom of the profile, so you never have to scroll to close it.
Main Menu: the main menu buttons are now carved stone slabs in the Enhanced Plus style, all one width.
Main Menu: on phones the buttons are a little more compact, so the whole menu now fits above the Screenshots and About buttons.
Website: the website now uses the game's stone and brass.
Field Bugs: FIELD BUGS 2026-10-07: the board crash, potion names, fishing, black screenshots, guild halls, skinning indoors
Puddles: WATER-NEXT + AUDIT WATER-NEXT: town puddles dried, the Enhanced water replaced (translucent, swell, shore foam, ripples), audited and its cost measured
Crafting: refining for a craft costs no extra station fee.
Materials: it never refines a material into a lower tier.
Crafting: when you are short of something, the box names the raw good you need (e.g. "short of Iron x2"), not the ingot.
Stores: when your Stores have no room for what it would refine, the box says so.
Crafting: if a refining step is refused, the message names the step where the chain stopped.
Repair Kits: materials you can't make yet are dimmed.
Repair Kits: the anvil's Weapons, Armour, Tools and Repair Kits are 39 pieces, not 308 rows behind a metal picker.
Repair Kits: the first-make bonus (+500 XP) is now paid once per piece per tier, not once per material.
Professions: a merged craft keeps the higher of its two XP totals.
Professions: each rank's choice is the higher craft's where it chose, else the other's.
Professions: a merged craft offers four choices at a rank, each named for the craft it acts on.
Professions: you may still take two crafts past Journeyman - now two of five.
Alchemy Station: the stations name the craft: "Building 10" at the workbench and the mason's bench, "Smithing 25" at the jeweller's bench, "Provisioning" at the fire and the alchemy station.

Smithing: temper at an anvil (Smithing) or a loom (Outfitting): a weapon, a piece of metal armour, leather armour or clothing, one quality step better - Crude to Standard, Standard to Fine, Fine to Superior.
Materials: a temper costs half the piece's recipe's main material, rounded up (a Steel Longsword: 2 Steel Ingots; a Leather Cuirass: 3 Cured Leather), needs that recipe's rank, and pays craft XP.
Market: a tempered piece gains condition and loses a little weight.
Sigils: legendary, Aetheric, artifact and Sigil pieces can't be tempered, and a Masterwork keeps its maker's quality.

Arcane Essence: reforge with Essence: from Enchanting 50, an enchanting station rolls one line of a known Magic piece again for 2 Arcane Essence, a Rare's for 5 - the Mages Guild's Reforge, paid in Essence.
Smithing: to temper or reforge a worn piece, take it off first
Repair Kits: Repair Kits made at an anvil now come in a quality, like other crafted pieces.
Repair Kits: the kit's card says its quality and how far it mends.
Repair Kits: Kits you already own, and field kits found in loot, work as before.
Town Layouts: Town ponds no longer show flat painted squares.
Town Layouts: six lone island tiles in town layouts are now dry ground, and some pond edges the puddle removal had wrongly cleared are back.
Dungeons: towns no longer sit in pits behind sheer walls of earth.
Coasts: coastal towns no longer stand behind cliffs at the beach line; the strand rises to them gently.
Coasts: towns on the coast stand on their own land, not dragged down toward the sea.
Terrain: rolling hills across the whole country, gentle in some regions and rolling hard in others, taller on the high ground.
Terrain: rivers and streams cut their own valleys: the water lies at the bottom, with the hills rising either side.
Terrain: mountains: long ridgelines that hold their line for kilometres, with spurs and smooth valleys.
Woods: mountain woods: foothills, half rolling and half ridges.
Terrain: the Alik'r: dune seas lying across the wind, a long rise to windward and a steep slip face to lee.
Terrain: rainforest: karst towers standing over plains.
Terrain: swamps: near-flat, with shallow hollows and low hummocks.
Woods: haunted woods: broken ground gashed by ravines and studded with crags.
Terrain: where climates meet, their lands blend across about a map pixel.
Roads: Roads and tracks no longer climb every hill.
Town Layouts: every player in a room stands on the same ground, even if a town pack failed to load for one of them.
Morrowind Body: the new steel armour set now moves with the Morrowind body the way Morrowind's own armour does.
Companions: your companions no longer follow you into the Burning Court.
Dungeon Map: selecting Info mode underground lights up, for six seconds, what is near, in sight and nameable (within 8 m), and a secrets tier also shows the hidden movers only a lever chain reaches

Dungeon Map: a lever that moves something out of sight tells which way, marking the spot on the dungeon map until found, with the mark glowing on arrival, and in Info mode its plaque says which way its work lies
Dungeon Map: the compass points back to the entrance along the trail walked, down a drop that was jumped but never back up one that cannot be climbed
Dungeon Map: optional exact quest guidance marks a quest's people and things on the dungeon map and the compass, and a finished quest's marks go away
Spells: Detect Treasure now also finds what is hidden in searched objects
Dungeon Map: secret walls are no longer labelled "Door"

Dungeon Sizes: online, every dungeon has its own size, small, medium or large, the same for everyone in it; small ones stay small, about half of all are medium, and the main story's dungeons and Abyss Dungeons are always large
Dungeon Sizes: a new offline option, Medium Dungeons, builds dungeons at a medium size of two interior blocks closed by six
Dungeon Sizes: a new offline option uses the online sizes offline, with a quest keeping the size it was set up at so quests started online keep their online sizes

Dungeons: online, a dungeon says what it is, Regular, Elite or Abyss Dungeon, with its size beside it (as in "Elite Dungeon, Small"), on the entrance sign, overworld name plates and sighting message, as a line on entering, and on the held map for the Bay's own dungeons
Abyss Dungeons: online, one rises at a time beside a busy city in the region with the most players online
Abyss Dungeons: a column of brass-gold light stands over it from the moment it rises, and the taverns of its city talk of it

Abyss Dungeons: the first player to reach its door finds it and everyone online hears where; from then its ring is on the map, its mark on the compass, and it has a row in the Timers window and a note on the notice board until it is gone

Abyss Dungeons: it is the hardest dungeon in the game: three foes at every spot, each four times as tough and hitting two and a half times as hard, six elite foes, half again the loot and no campfires

Abyss Dungeons: at its deepest point stands the Rift, a ring of brass light around a dark membrane, entered by pressing it or walking in, with a small Return beside it back to the way in; once the Remnant has fallen it takes no newcomers but those already through can step back in while the Hour collapses

Abyss Dungeons: the Rift leads to the Shattered Hour, the moment the Warp left behind: islands of stone and brass in a void under brass aurorae, the same sky for every player, with no rest, saving, map, Mark or Recall, regeneration or Levitate

Abyss Dungeons: the Orrery of Endings, the Shattered Hour's first hall, holds six Ending-stones to turn to the right hours using riddling Ledger plaques; every turn frays the Hour, which snaps back at 48 and lashes a quarter of health from those whose turns did not bring the stones nearer the Concord, and setting every stone right opens a bridge to the Unmoored Steps

Abyss Dungeons: the Unmoored Steps are a course of platforms over the void in three spans, the Drift, the Beat and the Crumble, each begun at a stone checkpoint; falling casts the player back to the checkpoint at some cost in health, never life

Abyss Dungeons: the Brass Remnant, a brass colossus kept from the Numidium, is fought in the arena of the Last Moment by everyone in the Hour at once, growing tougher with each fighter, through the Walking Hour, the Dragon Break and the Last Moment with a Reset to break Hearts against, and the Hour ends fifteen minutes after it wakes

Abyss Dungeons: each keeps one of six Endings and two of nine omens that change the Remnant's fight, said when found and shown on a card at its door and on entering the Hour, and its blows and burning brass take its element

Abyss Dungeons: everyone who truly fought the Remnant is credited an Hour broken, shown on the account and Inspect cards, each with a one-in-four chance of the Hourbreaker title and a one-in-eight chance of The Turning Hour aura, for accounts with a username only (a guest's Hour is kept for a week)

Brass of Numidium: a new Aetheric set of nine Dwarven brass pieces, all at the top of the Legendary range, with set bonuses Dwemer Brass, Gearward and The Hour Turns, carried only by the Brass Remnant's spoils one time in three

Abyss Dungeons: each fighter gets their own share of the Remnant's spoils: gold, a Rare piece (Legendary one time in four), two more Rare-or-better pieces, a Brass of Numidium piece one time in three and the Hourlock one time in fifty, with leftovers going into the pack on leaving
Abyss Dungeons: the Hour collapses three minutes after the Remnant falls, with a way home of pale light rising where it fell

Abyss Dungeons: dying in the Shattered Hour casts the player out for good, to wake before the Abyss Dungeon's door with the Rift closed to them, as the account's one life on every device and tab; when an Abyss Dungeon ends anyone still inside is put out at its door
Abyss Dungeons: the Hour has its own score of nine songs, one for each place and phase of the fight, each giving way to the next
Abyss Dungeons: the Remnant's steps, wind-ups and blows are heard where they happen, and the Hour has its own wind, ticking works, Orrery hum and drifting motes of brass

Abyss Dungeons: every blow bursts in sparks, shakes the arena and lights the floor, the colossus moves with its whole body, its gears fly, the Hour-Hand's beam sweeps the floor and title cards mark each turn of the fight
Abyss Dungeons: near a standing one the land's light and haze lean to brass, a banner at its door names it and how long it has, and its last hour is said to everyone online

Abyss Dungeons: a tab hidden through a landing no longer dodges it, a frozen page no longer holds a place in the fight, the Hardened Hearts omen and the Hearts' toughness are fair to small parties, and the Pulse never lands on top of the Reset
Abyss Dungeons: the fight runs smoother, making next to no garbage and building its effects before the first blow lands
Abyss Dungeons: the music no longer cuts out or plays the street's song between the Hollow's and the Hour's, the End sounds once and then tolls, and nothing plays war over the dead

Abyss Dungeons: the banner at its door fits a phone's screen, the title card stays clear of the Remnant's bar, times read the same everywhere, and the ring's card on the held map can be reached beside its city
Abyss Dungeons: a Resurrect in an ended one no longer strands the player there, and /unstuck in the Hour leaves by the Hour's own way home
Loot Rarity: Gilded is the new top of the rarity ladder, above Aetheric and Artifacts, with its name in gold leaf and a frame breathing light in every slot

Hourlock: a Gilded Thunderlock kept from a Dwemer smith's last commission, with fixed lines of +40% damage, +15 Agility, +30 Archery and +10 shock damage a shot, each at the top of the Legendary range
Hourlock: the Hour Tolls: every third shot that lands strikes for double, and a foe it fells gives back the pellet that felled it
Hourlock: it comes from the Brass Remnant's spoils one time in fifty, online

Hourlock: it lands about twice what any Legendary Thunderlock does a shot and is still the slowest weapon to fire; it cannot be broken down, reforged, honed, cursed, socketed or made an heirloom, its power sleeps in a duel, and its first find joins the codex at the head of the list
Dwarven Thunderlock: Dwemer Pellets are sold wherever weapons are, in Weapon Smiths, Armorers, General Stores and Pawn Shops, and restocked each day
Dwarven Thunderlock: the gun and its pellets show their own art in the pack, on the hotbar and in the quick slots instead of their initials, and a list shows the whole gun
Dwarven Thunderlock: the Morrowind 3D gun has no holes left, kicks back at the shot, and tips down and back up on reload with the breech heard after the bang
Abyss Dungeons: the Rift no longer stands in a sealed room with no way in; it stands at the deepest monster spawn point in the inner rooms
Abyss Dungeons: leaving the Shattered Hour after its Abyss Dungeon has ended no longer leaves the player hanging in the sky; they land where they stood outside when they went in
Abyss Dungeons: crew and sworn companions no longer follow the player through the Rift, waiting outside the Hour and returning when the player comes back, with a message that they cannot follow
Overworld: the dungeons near the player (Daggerfall's own, random dungeons online and a standing Abyss Dungeon) show their own entrance model, enlarged so they can be seen from above

Abyss Dungeons: stepping through the Rift no longer throws the player straight back out of the Shattered Hour, which happened on almost every try because the game spoke to the Hour's server before it had finished letting the player in
Abyss Dungeons: a connection that blinks during the boss fight no longer throws the player out of the Hour
Abyss Dungeons: leaving the Shattered Hour for any reason puts the player on the ground in front of the Abyss Dungeon's door, not hundreds of metres in the air above it
Abyss Dungeons: a tab left open from before the update puts the Rift in its old place, so reloading the page shows it where a friend sees it
Snowfall: in winter, outside the deserts, real snow lies on the ground, deeper in the wild than in towns, building up while snow falls and melting back in clear weather
Snowfall: the player, monsters, guards and townsfolk leave tracks in it, which slowly fill back in (faster while it snows) and are kept in the save
Snowfall: a fallen enemy leaves a hollow in the snow where it lay
Snowfall: with Basic Roads, paths and tracks keep only a thin layer of snow and main roads get a bank of snow along their edges
Snowfall: the winter ground under the snow has new textures
Wind: wind changes from day to day: trees and plants sway and shiver, some days turn windy or stormy, and gusts come and go with their own sound
Wind: leaves blow off the trees, and in winter snow blows off the boughs
Wind: the wind waits while the game is paused
Heat Haze: in the deserts by day the distant land and sky shimmer in the heat, fully under a clear sky and half as much under cloud, fading in after sunrise and out before sunset
Textures: the desert ground has new sand textures with ripples, from Sands of the Alik'r

Features: Snowfall, Windfall and Heat Haze are on by default in the enhanced outdoors, each with its own switch in Features, while the desert sand and winter ground are packs of their own on the Replacement packs card
Launcher: the launcher can be used with a controller: D-pad or left stick to move, A or Start to press, B to go back
Launcher: adding --play to the launch options (Playnite, Steam shortcuts, Big Picture) skips the launcher and goes straight into the game
Launcher: with --play, updates still arrive: the player is told in-game and they install on quit
Launcher: the launcher still opens when it needs to ask something, on the first run or if the Daggerfall folder cannot be found

Auctions: an auction won in a town whose seat takes a Tithe now closes on time and pays its seller, where it could stick when the seller's Marks were near the cap and twenty such sales held up every auction behind them
Auctions: auctions, guild writs and contracts settle on time on the service's own clock, even when nobody opens the market or the Work tab
Accounts: the letterbox, the count over a town's Notice Boards and the play time share one request to the account service instead of three, cutting its database work by about a third per player
Crouch: C now crouches and sneaks: while crouched the player moves at sneaking pace and stealth checks apply, so enemies are slower to notice them
Crouch: Left Alt no longer sneaks; the old standing sneak stays in Controls as an optional key with no key set by default
Crouch: players with their own saved key bindings see a one-time on-screen note that Sneak lost its key
Mode Wheel: holding Left Alt opens a wheel of interaction modes: Talk (up), Grab (right), Steal (down) and Info (left)
Mode Wheel: flicking the mouse toward a mode and letting go or clicking chooses it, and moving back to the middle cancels
Mode Wheel: F1 through F4 no longer change modes by default or open the browser's help or find bar, and can be bound back to the four modes in Controls
Mode Wheel: on a controller the d-pad's next mode still cycles through the modes
Cursor: on a controller the menu cursor eases in, speeds up on a long full push, slows over buttons and settles onto the nearest one on release
Cursor: the controller cursor works in every menu on both the Classic and Enhanced skins
Cursor: at the main menu the left stick moves the same cursor and A presses what it is on, while the d-pad still jumps from button to button
Cursor: Settings > Controls > Controller cursor assist > Off gives back Daggerfall's plain fixed-speed cursor
Cursor: clicking with the controller cursor no longer acts like a held-down drag in some windows

Spells: classic spellcasting runs at the same pace as the Morrowind animation, with the spell leaving the hands at half a second, so players with the Morrowind hands are no longer slower than everyone else
Spells: a new cast cannot start until the hands finish the motion, and clicking or recasting during it does nothing and costs nothing
Spells: casting speed scales with the Speed attribute, up to 25% faster at high Speed and 25% slower at low
Loot Rarity: a new rarity affix, +N% casting speed, rolls on jewellery and weapons and adds up across everything worn up to 30%, so classes that cannot wear plate can still get it
Wrothgarian Zone: the heart of the Wrothgarian Mountains is an open PvP zone marked on the world map with a red border and drifting fog, with Wrothgaria itself outside it

Wrothgarian Zone: other players in the zone, its dungeons included, can attack except the party, guild and duel opponent; attacking a player inside a city calls the guards, and the zone's guards are ten times as strong
Wrothgarian Zone: foes in the zone are four times as strong, elites and champions included, and travel in packs four times the size
Wrothgarian Zone: the zone has four tiers from the Foothills to the Heart, with loot rising +25%, +50%, +75% and +100% (twice the gold, drops and odds of a rare piece at the Heart)
Wrothgarian Zone: clicking the zone on the world map, or pressing V inside it, opens its own map showing the tiers, towns, dungeons and the player's position

Wrothgarian Zone: on death in the zone the player keeps potions, torches, campfire kit, food, ammunition and anything that never changes hands, while bags and the cart's load drop where they fell for 10 minutes, marked and open to anyone
Wrothgarian Zone: killed by another player, the killer may also take one piece of the victim's worn gear
Wrothgarian Zone: after dying in the zone the player waits two minutes to respawn in the nearest town outside it, and the cart comes too
Wrothgarian Zone: fast travel into or out of the zone is not allowed; inside it a fast journey costs 2,500 to 15,000 gold by the tier arrived in, once every 10 minutes
Wrothgarian Zone: travel speed in the zone is capped at x20 in the wilds and x40 on roads
Overworld: the Overworld no longer refuses a walk over mountains
Wrothgarian Zone: players outside the party and guild show as red nameless Strangers visible from 1.5 km, slowing travel more the closer they get
Wrothgarian Zone: /unstuck sends the player to the next town when outdoors, with a cooldown; in the zone it works only indoors, takes five minutes and can be cancelled

Wrothgarian Zone: each tier has two Greater Giants shown on the zone map where they wander, the same for everyone in the zone; at half health a Greater Giant calls ten giants, and giants never leave the zone

Wrothgarian Zone: the zone has its own dungeons, halls that change each day and cannot be re-entered for an hour after leaving unless the player's own remains are inside, marked by a lock on the map, with crows circling a hall where a player died
Wrothgarian Zone: banks, house purchases, world events and revenants are restricted in the zone, where only one revenant may walk with the player
Temples: temples offer Heal Curse beside Heal Disease
Resting: resting while poisoned or diseased warns the player first
Shop Screen: hovering an item in any shop shows the same card as in the inventory
Stats Card: the stats screen shows resistances
Dungeon Respawn: ordinary dungeons outside the zone respawn after 20 minutes and elite dungeons after 40
Tavern Cards: players can sit at a tavern's card table and play Texas Hold'em, with the tavern's regulars in the other chairs and the character seated for everyone to see
Tavern Cards: online the relay deals, owning the shuffle, hole cards and seat clock, so no client can see another's hand
Tavern Cards: gold tables take a buy-in of real gold, held in escrow by the account service and paid out on the hand's receipt, with top-ups between hands
Tavern Cards: the cards are physical on the cloth: dealt, fanned, peeked at, chips dragged to bet and the deck riffled

Iliac Hand: a two-player collectible card game played on the same table: three holdings between the players, six turns, hold two of three to win, with units, spells and Daedric Prince cards painted in code
Iliac Hand: every character carries a Card Binder from creation that holds their decks, and a Collections tab under Holdings shows the weapon codex and cards side by side
LeFay Monument: a monument to Julian LeFay stands in the middle of Gothway Garden, with three granite steps, a marble pedestal, a gilt-tipped obelisk and a bronze plaque on each side
LeFay Monument: looking at the monument offers Throw flowers or Read the inscription, and in Info mode a press reads the inscription

LeFay Monument: a thrown flower lands on the steps or at the foot on the player's side; each character keeps up to its 48 newest flowers through save and load, and the plaque counts how many were laid
LeFay Monument: townspeople walk around the monument
LeFay Monument: online, the player's flowers are theirs alone; others see the monument but not the flowers laid

Enhanced Maps: zooming the enhanced map out past the Iliac Bay shows the whole of Tamriel in the same hand, with nine provinces and borders, capitals, mountains, rivers and seas, and hovering reads the province, a capital or the sea; nothing beyond the Bay can be travelled to

Land Beyond the Bay: walking off the edge of the Iliac Bay, the land of Tamriel continues as hills, mountains and coasts under each province's own sky and trees, as empty ground with no towns, roads or dungeons yet
Features: the Tamriel on the map and Land beyond the Bay rows are on by default on the enhanced skin
Land Beyond the Bay: the world no longer freezes on its first outdoor build, which happened because the land beyond the Bay had pulled the online relay's code into the terrain worker
Enhanced Maps: the land beyond the Iliac Bay is traced from the game's own map of Tamriel (the race screen's picture), so the coast, provinces and borders are the ones Daggerfall drew
Enhanced Maps: the Bay is placed on that map by matching its own coastline, so the join is where the game put it
Land Beyond the Bay: the ground past the Bay's edge follows the same traced land
Tavern Cards: every tavern and inn has its own card table, a green-felt poker table with six stools standing near the entrance
Tavern Cards: pressing activate at the table sits the player down to play Hold'em with the regulars or with other players online
Tavern Cards: the tavern's ordinary dining tables are no longer card tables
Enhanced Maps: the land past the Iliac Bay is the shape Daggerfall's own map paints, one continent with the Imperial Province in the middle, not eight islands
Enhanced Maps: the Bay sits on it where its coastline matches
Townspeople: townsfolk inside a building spread through the whole room and sit at tables set apart, never at a table split by a wall, instead of bunching up by the door
Townspeople: nobody sits in the tavern for hours waiting for lunch
Townspeople: everyone in a room sees the same people in the same places, whether or not a door was left open
Town Watch: the watch posted at a city's gates stops strangers coming in and asks their business, and strangers answer civilly, curtly or with open hostility, with sellswords and sailors rougher
Town Watch: patrols stop strangers on their rounds
Townspeople: townsfolk fall out with each other, more often in the evening between drinkers, and the watch breaks it up
Townspeople: buyers haggle at stalls and beggars ask passers-by for a coin
Townspeople: when someone shouts, the people nearby fall quiet and turn to look
Townspeople: small voices fill the street: the night watch calls the hour with words for the weather, stalls cry their wares, beggars call out and drinkers sing on the way home from the tavern
Townspeople: every player in a town sees the same incidents at the same places
Town Watch: a stranger at the gate names their own home town, and a beggar no longer calls a stranger by name
Town Watch: every stranger stopped at a gate is questioned, and a gate stop no longer keeps a visitor from leaving town
Town Watch: the watch breaks up a quarrel even at a change of shift, and only one of a patrol pair calls the hour
Townspeople: a beggar no longer pulls a stall keeper away from their stall
Townspeople: beggars and stall keepers turn to face whoever they are talking to
Townspeople: people in an incident greet the player again once it is over
Townspeople: stall keepers no longer cry their wares before they reach the stall

Spellbook: the spellbook can no longer be dropped, put in a chest, pile or companion's pack, shift-dropped or sold at a shop, though it still goes into the player's own wagon, with the message "Your spellbook never leaves you."

Project Legacy: in an Enduring family a vampire, werewolf or wereboar who dies loses no years to Arkay's toll and always rises even with their span spent; once cured, the toll applies again from the next death
Wrothgarian Zone: a letter of credit is dropped at a death in the zone at its full value, like the purse's gold
Wallet: the wallet and the Deadlands Embers and Welkynd Shards it holds always stay with the player
Quests: every quest can now be abandoned and later reclaimed.
Quests: abandon asks you to click twice to confirm.
Quests: reclaim takes one click and works from the new Abandoned section.
Quests: an abandoned quest is set aside, not lost:
Quests: its timer stops;
Quests: its items, topics and journal are kept;
Quests: its dungeon or building stays reserved for it.
Quests: when you reclaim a quest, it picks up where you left it, and the days it spent abandoned don't count against its deadline.
Quests: abandoning a quest frees its quest-giver, so the guild offers you work again.
Quests: the game's built-in quests (the main quest's core, the curse and the tutorial) and sea raids can't be abandoned.
Quests: a reclaimed quest doesn't rejoin your party's shared progress.
Privateer's Hold: medium dungeons no longer repeat the same layout block twice.
Privateer's Hold: lord K'avar in Privateer's Hold: random quests no longer send you into main-story dungeons.
Privateer's Hold: enduring and Bloodlines characters can marry again.
Privateer's Hold: mercantile and Personality matter again when selling online.
Privateer's Hold: fast travel no longer drops you inside a mountain.
Privateer's Hold: enhanced Water can be switched off online.
Ships: the bank's ship loan has been removed.
Pause Menu: the pause menu now has a mailbox: an envelope beside the hourglass (online).
Pause Menu: when the developers send you a message, the envelope shows a count, and a line in the world chat tells you post has arrived.
Pause Menu: open a message to read it.
Pause Menu: type /mail in chat to open the mailbox from anywhere: outdoors, indoors or underground, on either menu style.
Pause Menu: a message whose item you haven't claimed can't be thrown away by mistake.
Abyss Dungeons: the thirteen players of the first Abyss Dungeon clear have been honoured:
Abyss Dungeons: a new title, Hour's First, drawn in rose gold, pearl and the white of dawn;
Abyss Dungeons: a new aura, The First Hour: The Turning Hour's wheel cast in the first dawn's light, with its dial turning forward, the Hour's own mark ablaze, and rays of first light;
Abyss Dungeons: the Hourlock, waiting for each of them in the mailbox.
Abyss Dungeons: wear the title and aura from your profile.
Snow: with Snowless Swamps and Jungles switched on, swamps and jungles no longer get deep snow on the ground or falling snow in winter.
Reach: deserts no longer get snow drifting in from nearby snowy regions, and the edge of the desert next to a snowy area stays bare.
Front Door: you can now decorate the ground right outside your own front door.
Performance: opening the Overworld no longer freezes the game: nearby dungeon models now load one per frame once the view has finished rising.
Performance: long journeys no longer slowly use up video memory.
Performance: deep snow no longer does its work while the Overworld is open, since none of it is shown there.
Performance: saving is faster in snowy areas: the snow-track data is only recompressed when it has changed.
Ships: fixed a crash ("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'velocity')") when another player's ship list changed while you stood on one of their ships.
Houses: when a member of your family dies for good, their houses pass to whoever carries the line on - door, bed, chests and furniture as they left them.
Houses: online, a fallen character's home moves to their heir, cupboards included.
Houses: if your heir already owns a house in that region, the inherited one waits until they sell theirs.
Characters: card tables locked players out.
Characters: the red table plays for gold, and only realm characters can stake at it.
Characters: realm characters can now also play for chips at the green table, alongside everyone else.

Banners: whenever a Rare, Legendary, Aetheric, Artifact or Gilded item reaches your pack, wagon or Materials Bag, a banner slides in at the right edge of the screen: the item's picture framed in its tier colour, its tier and pips, its name, and what it is.

Banners: it works however the item arrives: loot, boss and raid spoils, quest rewards, crafting, the Sigil Broker, shops, trades, the market, and Iliac cards (shown with their own card face and a count when you get several).
Banners: aetheric, Artifact and Gilded items get a bigger, glowing banner and a fanfare.
Banners: up to three banners show at once, newest on top; more wait their turn, best tier first.
Banners: moving items between your pack, wagon and bag, or taking your own things back out of storage, never shows a banner.
Banners: a first find for your codex now shows "New to your codex" on its banner instead of a separate line.
Banners: the small pickup feed under the crosshair no longer repeats an item its banner is announcing.
Banners: move or hide the banners in the HUD editor (Alt+U): Loot banners.
Realm: at the red (gold) table, if the realm can't take your stake, the panel now says why, beside the buy-in.
Land Beyond the Bay: clicking a spot on the Overworld while you're past the edge of the Iliac Bay no longer crashes the game ("RangeError: invalid array length").
Logging: online, a player beyond the Bay is no longer invisible.
Town Map: a Dark Brotherhood or Thieves Guild member's hall stays named on the town map and at its door while you have a contract.
Market: looted weapons, armour, clothing and jewellery can be listed on the market, sold at stalls and traded again.
Motherlodes: motherlodes, veins, boulders, herbs and trees no longer appear inside rocks.
Talk Window: the carriage driver at one gate of each walled city (Shrarton in Tasoparet) now has a face in the talk window.
Spellcasting: the casting hands are quick again: a spell leaves your hands 0.2 seconds after you cast it, as it did before the casting speed change.
Spellcasting: spells still can't be spammed.
Spellcasting: the thin dotted line that showed up beside the casting hands on some graphics cards is gone.
Dungeons: if two players' dungeons were built differently (usually one of you on an older version), you now see the host's monsters instead of fighting ones nobody else can see.
Online Foes: other players' monsters keep up better while they run, so you're less likely to swing at the air where a monster used to be.
Online Foes: more of another player's summoned and called monsters are shown, including all ten of a Greater Giant's call.
Quests: quest monsters are visible to everyone nearby, and anyone can hit them.
Wrothgarian Zone: after you die, your own pile of remains now shows up.
Wrothgarian Zone: a red "My remains" waypoint marks where your remains lie, on both the Overworld and the world map, and goes away when they do.
World of Daggerfall: the giant angular rock spires from World of Daggerfall's mountains are off by default.
World of Daggerfall: boulders in rock fields no longer hang over slopes with their open undersides showing.
Launcher: the Discord links on the website, the Terms and Privacy pages, and the desktop launcher now point to our new invite: https://discord.gg/jM2JdwSM8w
Standing: the Rift is now a brass astrolabe standing in a cracked crater, turned to face down its hall's longest line.
The Rift: its iris shows its state.
The Rift: through the iris you see the Hour's own sky, with real depth as you move.
Silver: the Return is a pale stone arch with silver bands and a window home: the sky over the Hollow's city at the world's real hour, with Masser and Secunda at night.
Silver: a silver hand-plate on every Return's sill lights up when you aim at it.
Stepping Through: entering the Hour has its own transition: twelve brass blades close over the Rift wherever it is on your screen and lock into a clock face.
Silver: leaving by the way back or the Return, the clock is silver and still cracked.
Stepping Through: if your system is set to reduce motion, the face holds still and fades in and out instead.
Stepping Through: when you arrive in the Hour, the way back breathes out a spray of brass sparks and its ring turns once.
Compass: the light has been redone, so floors read as stone and brass instead of one amber glow.
The Shattered Hour: The islands hang in the void on jagged rock spires, with half-buried gears and chains swaying on the clock's tick.

Hanging: the sky is hand-painted: dithered bands of void, single-pixel stars, aurorae, a great clock face drawn in stars with its numerals and the six Endings as constellations, and the Bay's cities hanging upside down with their windows lit.
The Shattered Hour: The way back looks into the hall you came from: dark coursed stone lit gold from the front.
The Shattered Hour: The arena tells you the fight through its floor.
The Shattered Hour: The Stomp's ring now rises as a low wall of brass light you can see to jump.
Lantern: the arena's four pillars are clock-towers now.
Helm: the Brass Remnant has been rebuilt from riveted brass plate.
The Shattered Hour: The Remnant shows what it's about to do.
Standing: a great dial on its back keeps the fight's time: it ticks backwards, runs down a stun, and spins back to twelve on the Reset.
The Shattered Hour: when it falls, its heart tears out and rises before going dark, and the dial breaks free and rolls away.
Silver: where it falls, the way home assembles inside a column of pale light: the jambs rise out of the floor, the arch swings shut, and the keystone clock drops into place.
Climb: every step shows what it will do next.
The Unmoored Steps: crumble stones crack in stages under your feet, fall in pieces, and fly back together when they return.
The Unmoored Steps: a vane on the last island swings toward the next gust a second before it hits.
The Unmoored Steps: waystones mark where the void will send you back, and a golden burst plays in reverse when it does.
Orrery of Endings: The six stones are rebuilt: carved shafts with their sign, a dial in a bezel, and a gear on top that turns with the hand.
Banners: Banners hang from each stone, lecterns hold the plaques' ledgers, and the floor's dial is raised in brass, its lit plates glowing like soul gems.
Orrery of Endings: six rings turn slowly overhead, shivering as the Hour frays.
Abyss Dungeons: changing weapons or casting on an ally right after a connection blip no longer throws you out of the Hour.
Abyss Dungeons: hiding the tab no longer dodges the Pulse, the Reset or the End.
Abyss Dungeons: a fighter whose connection dropped while a fight was lost can rejoin the next fight instead of being stuck.
Abyss Dungeons: you can no longer set a Mark inside an Abyss Dungeon.
Abyss Dungeons: stepping into the Rift now works on slow machines and across a hitch.
Abyss Dungeons: pressing near the Rift no longer grabs it when you're aiming at a body or the floor.
Abyss Dungeons: the Return and the landing back from the Hour no longer stand on or next to the Rift in small rooms.
Abyss Dungeons: the Rift is sized to fit its hall and no longer pokes through pillars or ceilings.
Abyss Dungeons: Abyss Dungeons no longer appear on beaches or with their end underwater.
Abyss Dungeons: a refused or failed step through the Rift leaves you in front of the Hollow's door instead of in its middle.
Abyss Dungeons: an open door no longer moves where the Rift stands from one player to the next.
Abyss Dungeons: the Remnant no longer grunts while it's outside time, a Stomp lands as one thud instead of two, and the Hour's distant sounds stop when you leave.
Abyss Dungeons: coming back to the tab no longer plays every Heart that broke while you were away all at once.
Brass of Numidium: the Brass of Numidium's powers play the right sounds.
Abyss Dungeons: the fight's title cards only show near the arena.
Abyss Dungeons: the Remnant's health bar uses the Hour's own colours.
Abyss Dungeons: after the Concord, a stone's plaque says "The Concord holds." instead of offering a turn.
Abyss Dungeons: the large boat no longer shares its textures with the Shattered Hour.
Abyss Dungeons: the Rift's and the Return's textures sit where they belong: the Return's stone and dial were drawing in the Rift's brass, and four of the ring's numerals showed the wrong picture.
Abyss Dungeons: levitate no longer works in the Shattered Hour.
Abyss Dungeons: you can no longer walk onto the Concord's bridge before it has finished laying.
Abyss Dungeons: the Drift's pendulum rods hang beside its platform instead of through anyone standing at its edge.
Abyss Dungeons: the sky and the arena no longer turn red before a fight has started.
Abyss Dungeons: the way back no longer rings a bell every time you arrive, and its light stays on the island instead of spilling into the void.
Abyss Dungeons: the arrival sparks wait until the step-through animation finishes, and play on every arrival, not only the first.
Abyss Dungeons: the Hollow and the Hour run with less memory churn: the Rift, the sky, the Orrery's hands and the Hour's sounds no longer allocate every frame.
Features: settings and Features are now one screen, in tabs: Graphics, Gameplay, Combat, World, Interface, Audio, Controls, Accessibility, Mods & files.
Settings: graphics opens on a quality preset: Low, Medium, High or Ultra.
Mods: one search across every tab.
Restore: each tab can restore its own defaults. "Reset everything to defaults" resets every setting and mod.
Mods: Mods & files lists every mod and takes you to its options.
Settings: less text.
Death Screen: quick-loading (F11) after dying in town no longer leaves the death screen up.
Paperdoll: face mods (Paperdoll Enhanced) draw faces at their proper size.
Morrowind Asset Pack: updated steel armour model: wider breastplate shoulders, larger pauldrons, and the waist band is its own piece.
Helm: the steel helm (closed and open) now sits properly on your head.
Morrowind Models: Morrowind models (your body, arms, armour, weapons and item pictures) now use smooth shading instead of a faceted look.
Oblivion Gates: the Oblivion Gate is a new, handcrafted model: two clawed pillars under a heavy lintel, ringed with burning spines.
Oblivion Gates: its stone is cracked basalt veined with fire.
Oblivion Gates: the portal's fire now fills the gate's opening right to the stone, and it meets the ground even on a slope.
Oblivion Gates: the gate rises fully out of the ground, with no piece of it showing early on a hillside.
Oblivion Gates: anyone caught inside the stone as the gate finishes rising is set down safely in front of it, wherever they stood.
Burning Court: the portal on the bridge is gone.
Burning Court: the way home opens where the Warden falls, as before, and now closes as the court comes apart.
Burning Court: until he falls, the only ways out are death and the Wrath. /unstuck no longer works inside the court.
Burning Court: if the fight stops answering (a full or stalled room), you are returned to Tamriel after 20 seconds instead of being stranded.
Oblivion Gates: iliac Hand at the tavern table.
Oblivion Gates: offline, against the tavern's regulars.
Oblivion Gates: play for fun, or for keeps: each side stakes a card and the loser hands it over.
Oblivion Gates: online, against another player at the same table.
Oblivion Gates: ranked, for realm characters on a registered account.
Oblivion Gates: where cards come from:
Oblivion Gates: a slain creature sometimes drops its own card (a rat drops a Rat).
Oblivion Gates: a finished guild, temple or knightly-order quest pays one of that guild's cards about one time in three.
Oblivion Gates: card Packs are sold at Enhanced taverns' counters and card tables.
Oblivion Gates: three new boss cards: the Oblivion Gate's Warden, Sethrakul, and the Abyss Dungeon's Brass Remnant.
Oblivion Gates: at the Hold'em table:
Oblivion Gates: press your cards and pull down to squeeze them.
Oblivion Gates: click your cards to check, or push them up the screen to fold on your turn.
Oblivion Gates: other players seated at a card table now sit in their chairs instead of standing in them.
Iliac Hand: realm customs counts cards.
Iliac Hand: Iliac Hand's panel can be played with the keyboard.
Tavern Cards: Tavern card tables no longer stand across doorways; they keep a walking lane clear.
Tavern Cards: ghost and other flying companions no longer climb into the ceiling while following, and their health bar shows again.
Tavern Cards: your PvP remains stay marked on the map if the game crashes or closes before you reach them.
Tavern Cards: firefox for Android: tapping the screen no longer opens the pause menu.
Tavern Cards: the Stores page now lists looted, shop-bought or traded materials as "unstorable" and explains why they can't go in.
Online Characters: every save the realm takes from an online character is now read by the server, not only the first.
Online Characters: nothing you play is ever lost to this.
Online Characters: if the same valuable item turns up on two characters, the character that showed it second is the one checked; the original owner keeps theirs and can still sell it.
Online Characters: enchanted items brought into the realm from a classic Daggerfall save through customs stay yours, but can't be traded or sold in the realm.
Online Characters: the server now records how fast each character's wealth grows against time actually played.
Shops: items handed to you by other players (chests, bodies, shops) are now checked the same way.
Repairs: items in for repair could be refused when passed between players; that's fixed.

Crafting Stations: every crafting station now uses the materials in your Materials Bag and pack, not just your Stores: the anvil, forge, workbench, loom, mason's bench, cook fire, jeweller's bench, alchemy and enchanting stations, and tempering.
Crafting: that includes materials you looted, bought at a shop, were traded, or took out of your Stores before the bag existed.
Crafting: a craft that needs refining first (ore to ingots, logs to charcoal) plans that from your bag too.
Materials: when a station takes something from your pack, any of it you didn't gather or take out of your Stores is kept as "from your pack".
Materials: goods from your pack can only be used at a crafting station, or taken back out into your pack.
Materials: a piece crafted from them sells on the market for gold only, the same as any piece from your pack.
Mining: mountain and Mountain Woods veins can now be Silver on ground few players have mined.
Mining: gold, Platinum, Mithril and a region's own ore still appear only once three different players (each account at least a week old) have gathered on that ground.
Maps: new setting: Settings → Interface → Maps → Map text and icons - Auto, or 0.75× to 2×.

Coasts: the map of Tamriel beyond the Iliac Bay is traced more faithfully: provinces meet at their borders instead of across thin channels of sea, specks of paint are no longer drawn as tiny lakes, coastlines are smooth, the continent lines up with the Bay's own coast, and the made-up rivers that ran out to sea are gone.
Character Sheet: new setting: Settings → Interface → Character sheet → Every faction's standing (off by default).
Beautiful Villages: Beautiful Villages: in Akatosh's temple villages (Gentle Redeemer of Akatosh in Wayrest among them) one house stood buried inside a hill.
Textures: ebony armour now has its own full set on the Morrowind-style body: breastplate with tassets, pauldrons, gauntlets, greaves, boots and helm, each with its own painted texture.
Ebony Armour: mithril and Adamantium still wear the Morrowind ebony look.
Cloaks: casual and Formal Cloaks are now real cloaks, worn over your armour instead of a full robe that hid it.
Cloaks: the cloak moves with your body: it hangs from the shoulders and swings with your legs as you walk.
Cloaks: each dye has its own colour.
Cloaks: the cloak is smooth over the shoulders.
Inventory: its inventory icon shows the cloak itself.
Weapons: greatswords and bows worn on the back sit over the cloak and stay visible.
Weapons: swords, daggers and crossbows at the hip hang under it.
Weapons: stowed weapons follow the cloak as you walk, run and lean, so they no longer cut through it.
Weapons: sitting at a card table, the cloak hangs behind you instead of folding under your legs.
Standing: online, your reputation with all twenty-two guilds, temples and knightly orders is kept by the realm, not your save.
Standing: reputation can rise by up to 15 a day with each guild.
Standing: ranks 0 to 7 work exactly as in Daggerfall, earned with reputation and skill.
Court Writs: each chapter posts hall writs on its town's Notice Board, under the Work tab.
Court Writs: a hall writ pays like a Court writ, plus +2 reputation with the guild.
Court Writs: members also get their own writ each day, one per guild, which earns Merit for the chapter.
Court Writs: the Thieves Guild's and the Dark Brotherhood's writs are shown to their members alone.
Reputation: slaying a gate's guardian or defending a raided town earns +1 reputation with each guild you belong to that keeps a chapter there.
Receipts: a chapter's receipt writ gives +2 more for your first such deed of the day in that region.
Notice Board: merit is what members earn for their chapter: 100 for a member's own writ (only units you gathered yourself count, not bought ones), and a share of 50 for each receipt.
Notice Board: you can earn up to 600 Merit a week at a chapter.
Notice Board: every week at the Turning, each chapter's Strength (0 to 100, starting at 50) rises with its members' Merit and slips when they neglect it.
Notice Board: a chapter's Strength sets its standing:
Notice Board: failing (0–19): training and spells a quarter dearer, a poorer shelf, fewer writs.
Notice Board: steady (20–69): Daggerfall's own prices and shelf.
Notice Board: thriving (70–89) and Ascendant (90–100): training and spells a tenth cheaper, a richer shelf, more writs.
Notice Board: the Notice Board shows each chapter's standing ("The chapter of the Fighters Guild here is Thriving").
Seats: each chapter has one Master (rank 9) and three officers (rank 8).
Seats: to hold a seat you need 80 reputation, fourteen days in the guild, an account at least a week old, and rank 7 earned the usual way.
Seats: a sitting holder keeps the seat on a tie.
Seats: at its own chapter's halls a seat gives you rank 8 or 9: its title, services and quests.
Seats: titles on your name: Master, Officer, and Former Master for the rest of the Season you lost the seat in.
Seats: a Master names the chapter's Focus each week: the kind of material its hall writs ask for more of.
Hall of Records: the Hall of Records keeps each region's Chronicle: every seat that changed hands, every Season's ending and every patron.
Guild Hall: the first book on every guild hall's shelf is now the hall's roll: its chapter's standing, its Master and its officers.
A Living Hall: A thriving chapter's hall is busier.
Seasons: townsfolk talk about their chapters, whether they're failing, thriving, or caught up in a Season's trouble.
Seasons: calm: a quiet Season.
Seasons: schism: two of the hall's people stand for different doctrines: cheaper training, a deeper shelf, or more writs.
Seasons: succession: the hall's head steps down.
Seasons: crackdown: the watch hunts the chapter.
Seasons: rivalry: two rival chapters in one region race for Merit, and the winner takes 10 Strength from the loser.
Seasons: decline: the chapter loses 2 Strength a week unless its members earn twice the usual target.
Seasons: ascendancy: the halls' training and spells are a further tenth off, and the Master is a High Master for the Season.
Seasons: a Master who holds the seat for an entire Season earns Season Master ("Master of the Mages Guild, Daggerfall, Season 3") for good.
Notice Board: the Notice Board and the hall's roll tell each chapter's Season.
Seasons: a player guild's guildmaster can bid silver from the guild's treasury to become a chapter's patron for the next Season.
Seasons: when the Season opens, the highest bid wins and is spent.
Banners: a patron's banners hang beside the chapter's halls, and its members pay the Thriving price there whatever the chapter's standing.
Influence: patronage buys no influence over the seats.
Seasons: the Thieves Guild's and the Dark Brotherhood's chapters, writs, Seasons and seats are shown to their members alone.
Relay: the relay passes on each player's movement faster when many players are together: with 200 players in one spot a movement update costs 47 µs instead of 82, and 50 instead of 96 at 256.
Performance: online, the frame no longer stalls while the living world works out its travellers' roads.
Performance: the sun's shadows check each object once instead of once per shadow layer: about 0.6 ms a frame saved in a town by day, and the same shadows as before.
Performance: the movable HUD checks its layout four times a second instead of about eight.
Wrothgarian Zone: cast-When-Held gear no longer breaks from re-equipping.
Wrothgarian Zone: a Bloodline is never locked out after a failed heir's birth online.
Wrothgarian Zone: your own remains in the Wrothgarian zone now show up.
Duels: Duels are now judged by the server.
Duels: your health bar in a duel is the duel's own vitality.
Duels: both duellists' bars now show as soon as the bout starts, not only after the first hit.
Duels: wins and losses are recorded from the server's result.
Battle: fights in the zone are judged by the server the same way duels are.
Wrothgarian Zone: your vitality goes back to full only after 30 seconds with nobody hitting you, spent in the zone.
Wrothgarian Zone: a fallen player stays down for the full two minutes.
Characters: when you fall to another player, the server takes what you drop from your saved character and puts it in your remains.
Pack: if your pack holds more than your remains can carry, the gold and your most valuable pieces go into the remains first, and the rest stays with you.
Pack: the piece your killer picks off your body now arrives in their pack by itself once your remains appear.
Wrothgarian Zone: if the fallen player never settles their death within 30 seconds, the killer's game does it for them, and lays the remains where the body fell.
Wrothgarian Zone: a crafted piece you pick back up from your own remains can still be worn, but it can't be traded or sold any more.
Wrothgarian Zone: party members, and anyone who left your party in the last ten minutes, still can't hurt you there.
Royal Tourney: every damaging spell cast at another player is capped by the server: at most three in five seconds, each to its limit.
Royal Tourney: a Royal Tourney bout is blows only.

Abyss Dungeons: the world events channel now announces Abyss Dungeons: when one rises (never where - it still has to be found), when someone finds it and in which region, when the Hour is broken and by whom, and when a found one fades unbroken.
Abyss Dungeons: the rise and the find ping the world events role, so you hear when there is one to hunt and when its Rift is open.
Cover: steel and Ebony pauldrons now fully cover the upper arm - no more skin showing through.
Cover: the closed Steel helm and the Ebony helm sit lower, where they were designed to, and the Ebony helm's mail coif covers the neck again.
Wagon: the Small Cart is now drawn as the new Wagon Cart.
Wagon: two new wagons are for sale at General Stores:
Wagon: the Open Wagon (900 gold) carries 1500 kg and has four seats in the back.
Wagon: the Caravan (2500 gold) carries 2000 kg and you can step inside it.
Wagon: if you own more than one wagon, you drive the best one, and your wagon store holds what that wagon holds.
Wagon: Wagon wheels now turn as the wagon moves and turn back when you reverse.
Wagon: you can't sell, trade, list, or put in a guild vault a wagon you're driving while its store holds goods.
Wagon: online, you can choose Ask to ride on another player's Open Wagon.
Fast Travel: once seated, you go where the wagon goes, fast travel included, with no fare.
Wagon: jump gets you down.
Companions: your companions take the seats no player is using.
Companions: riders and companions are drawn in the wagon in the Overworld too.
Houses: inside, the caravan is a room of its own, shaped like the caravan.
Decor: place decor.
The Caravan: craft at stations.
Stores: store things.
The Caravan: rest.
Wagon: paint your wagons for free, any time.
Guilds: online, set Who may enter, like an online home: Only me, My party, My guild or Anyone.
The Caravan: a save or Recall made inside a caravan that can't be re-entered now puts you outside its rear door.
Houses: from the street, house windows show a room behind the glass.
Houses: from inside a house or your caravan, windows show the real street outside, at the current time of day, in the current weather, with the sea where there is one.
Bow: with Draw And Release Bows off, holding attack fires again each time the bow is ready at the same rate as before, so spam-clicking is no longer needed
Bow: under the Morrowind bow a click while the bow was still being drawn no longer fires two arrows from one draw and then draws with no arrow; each click is one draw and one arrow
Bow: the arrow leaves on the release, no longer flying off at the start of the draw or halfway through it

Bow: the Morrowind bow draws properly: the nocked arrow travels to the string and is drawn back and the bow's limbs and string bend with the draw, where before the bow stayed rigid and the arrow sat in its resting spot
Gem Sockets: weapons carry visible sockets, shown as round wells under the picture on the item card and as small pips along the top of the tile in the pack

Gem Sockets: a weapon's size sets how many sockets it can have: one on a short blade (dagger, tanto, shortsword, wakizashi), two on a one-handed weapon and three on a two-handed weapon, a bow or the Thunderlock, while armour and jewellery keep their single socket
Gem Sockets: socketed weapons drop far more often, Magic weapons can have one socket, and Rare and Legendary weapons can roll extra sockets up to their size
Gem Sockets: gems are set from the pack by clicking an empty socket to pick a gem, or by choosing Set in... on a gem's card; setting is free apart from the gem being spent and works on a worn weapon
Gem Sockets: clicking a filled socket twice shatters its gem, and the Mages Guild's Reforge extracts a gem whole for gold based on its grade
Gem Sockets: a piece that holds a gem is never salvaged until the gem is extracted or unset, and a set gem adds its own worth to the piece's price

Gems: each of the eight classic gems comes in five grades, Chipped, Flawed, regular, Flawless and Perfect, with better grades giving stronger bonuses: fire or frost damage, life leech, extra damage or an attribute in a weapon, and a resistance or an attribute in armour or jewellery
Gems: gems drop from bodies, dungeon treasure and tavern or guild caches, with deeper and deadlier places dropping better grades

Gems: world bosses drop gems, one from the Oblivion Gate's Warden, one to every player who dealt their share of the damage to Sethrakul, and two from the Brass Remnant, all Flawless or Perfect, and the bosses' weapons and armour can come socketed

Gems: a weapon's gems of the same kind together give at most one Rare line's worth (for example +6 Fire damage at most), mixing kinds pays more than doubling up, and the item card shows when a weapon hits the limit

Dungeon Scaling: monsters are tougher depending on where they are met, using the grading that decides a place's loot: mines, natural caves, cemeteries and towns add nothing, the strongest foes in a Crypt get up to a third more health and in a Vampire Haunt up to 70% more, and in a Dragon's Den or the Volcanic Caves up to double health, hitting up to 25% harder and with more skill
Foes: the wilderness is a little tougher by day and more so at night
Dungeon Scaling: the weaker the creature the less it gains, with rats, bats and imps gaining nothing, and offline, turning off Loot rarity turns the scaling off too

Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul: with the overhaul on (the default) an enemy's weapon skill helps it hit exactly as much as the player's helps them, and its critical strikes land as often and hit as hard as the player's

Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul: a weapon in top condition no longer strikes up to 30% harder and fresh armour no longer lets 15% less damage through unless the overhaul's Equipment Damage Enhanced module is turned on, which wears gear down fast enough to make the bonus something earned by maintenance; worn gear still hits weaker and blocks less

Elites: elite enemies appear offline while Loot rarity is on, about one foe in twenty in the wilds and sometimes one in a dungeon, never a creature below level 3, so a level-1 or level-2 character meets none among a dungeon's bandits and knights
Enhanced AI: is on by default offline, as it already was online, and can be switched back to the classic enemy AI in Settings > Combat > Enemies; pressing All off in the features list keeps it off
Death Penalty: dying offline costs gold: when Project Legacy raises the player after a death they lose a tenth of the gold they carry, as online, while gold in the bank is safe
Death Screen: shows the amount of gold lost and says Rise instead of "End the journey"
Wagon Yards: every city and town has a Stable and a Wagon Yard, open-air yards on the town's open ground clear of homes, guild halls and roads
Wagon Yards: the Stable sells horses and buys them back
Wagon Yards: the Wagon Yard sells and buys back the Small Cart, the Open Wagon and the Caravan
Wagon Yards: each yard has its own keeper named for the town and a signboard, with horses and wagons on show and pressing one opening the yard's stock
Wagon Yards: General Stores no longer sell or buy horses, carts or wagons
Wagon Yards: the Open Wagon costs 9000 gold and the Caravan 25000, and wagons bought before the change stay valid everywhere
Wagon Yards: every yard charges the same price in every region and its keepers cannot be stolen from
Wagon Yards: yards keep clear of the boulders, stalls, walls and crop fields the town mods add and of the spots where travellers arrive
Wagon Yards: a town's yards can be seen through the windows of nearby houses
Wagon: on the Open Wagon and the Caravan the player sits on the driver's bench with the reins in hand
Wagon: the Open Wagon and the Caravan need a team of two horses, the second bought at a Stable, while the Small Cart still takes one
Wagon: the horses are harnessed with traces and reins that sag and swing as the wagon moves
Wagon: zooming out to third person works while driving from the bench on the Open Wagon as well as the Caravan, and stays after fast travel or a teleport
Wagon: a parked wagon blocks the player instead of letting them walk through it
Wagon: with one horse left for a two-horse wagon the player can ride that horse again
Wagon: wagons are no longer oversized in the Overworld
Wagon: summoning a wagon no longer traps the player under it
Wagon: other players driving a bench wagon are drawn sitting on their bench
Bounty Boards: clicking Take bounty repeatedly takes the board's notices in order from the top, where the just-taken notice used to stay open with Give up under the cursor and be handed straight back
Bounty Boards: after the last take the notice shows a short line instead of buttons, to share or give up from the left, and in a party a stray click no longer shares the bounty with everyone
Bounty Boards: Give up asks for a second click ("Click again to give up") and sits on the left of the notice
Bounty Boards: the board keeps one size, so the Take button stays put while the list grows

World Map: the Enhanced world map opens on the player as if Find me were pressed, gliding to where they stand with the red cross blinking, while opening from the journal, a journey, a teleport and a carriage or ship driver's map work as before and the classic map is unchanged
Townspeople: towns in Hammerfell's regions are walked by Redguards, who keep their names but get Redguard looks, including townsfolk inside houses with Variant Residents on (the default)

Damned Weapons: one cursed Legendary weapon in four is Damned, its curse line rolling at the very top of its range but costing 8 health on every hit, with no temple able to lift the curse and the bleeding stopping once it is unequipped
Arena Bouts: an enchantment's own bite, a Damned blade's or any Health Leech weapon's, no longer kills the player in arena bouts but leaves them at 1 health like every other blow there

Boss Fight Integrity: in Oblivion Gate, Abyss Dungeon and Sea Serpent fights the server checks the boss's attacks itself, working out from where the player stood which blows reached them while the game still shows each hit

Boss Fight Integrity: the server keeps its own count of each fighter's health in these fights and of each ship's hull against the serpent, updated as the game reports it, with potions, healing spells and repairs counting within a set amount over time and allies' healing spells not using that amount
Boss Fight Integrity: sailing off to repair a ship and returning to the serpent makes the server count the hull fresh

Boss Fight Integrity: for now the server only records this: nobody is knocked down or wrecked by it and fights play as before, until staff switch it on once a week of fights shows how much healing honest players really use
Boss Fight Integrity: once switched on, a fighter the server counts as fallen will fall in their own game too, using up the one life in the Abyss Dungeon and wrecking the ship at sea

Boss Fight Integrity: the server gives the benefit of the doubt: a blow counts only if the player was well inside the attack's area both just before and just after it landed, and elemental damage never counts because resistances can block it
