Wagon: third person works properly when driving the Open Wagon or the Caravan from its bench, the camera swinging up over the wagon's roof so the player can zoom out and look down at the driver, the team and the road, where before it jammed into the character's head
Wagon Yards: both town maps show each town's Stable and Wagon Yard, their ground in the shop colour with their names written on
Wagon Yards: the Overworld marks each Stable with a horseshoe and each Wagon Yard with a wheel, with their names, and they hide with the Towns filter
Wagon Yards: asking anyone "Where is..." offers new Stables and Wagon yards lists, and townsfolk give directions or mark them on the map as for any shop

Performance: towns full of furnished yards are cheaper to draw, with yard pieces behind the player no longer drawn and many copies of the same placed piece no longer forcing extra shadow work every frame
Performance: the stables and wagon yards in every visible town are no longer drawn when behind the player or far out of view

Performance: collision no longer gets more expensive as the view distance is raised, so movement for the player and every nearby foe costs about the same at Ultra as at Low, including while new land loads
Performance: a lamp's shadow no longer redraws all six of its sides when someone walks past, only the sides they are in front of
Performance: other players' name tags are cheaper for the browser to move when the camera turns in a crowd
Performance: the game's main per-frame loop runs as optimized code in the browser

Accounts: reconnecting after a server update asks less of the account service: when world chat was too busy to let the player straight in, the game reuses the sign-in token it has instead of asking for a fresh one on every retry
Accounts: the account service can answer sign-in token requests from Cloudflare's database read replicas
Live Chat: the world chat server does less work for each player who joins or leaves, and that work grows far less with the number of players online
Live Chat: the World tab's Online count stays accurate once more than 512 players are in the world chat, where it used to creep upward
Live Chat: a World tab closed because the player went online on another device no longer shows the old count over an empty list

Morrowind People: with the Morrowind body on, the people and creatures around the player stand in Morrowind bodies too: dungeon and wilderness foes, the city watch, townsfolk, people in buildings and dungeons, quest givers, the keepers of the Stables and Wagon Yards, ship crews, siege fighters, road parties and the Oblivion Gate's boss and his host
Morrowind People: foes wear the armour and carry the weapons they rolled, and each has a race and face of its own
Morrowind People: online, everyone sees a foe as its owner does, with the same race, face, armour and weapon, and in a dungeon each player's copy of a foe carries and wears that player's own loot

Morrowind People: townsfolk are dressed by their station, priests in robes, nobles in formal wear, merchants, scholars and the town's guards in steel, and in a living town people wear what their sprite shows, such as the watch's uniform on duty and a guild's or priests' class gear
Morrowind People: foes swing, flinch when struck and fall when they die, and their tells show on the body too: the wind-up glint, the elite glow, the hit flash and the dissolve
Morrowind People: a body is drawn at its sprite's size, so elites stand larger and the wild zone's giants tower over the player, and the dead lie where their corpse lies, on a moving deck too

Morrowind People: creatures use Morrowind's creatures where Daggerfall's have a match (rats, skeletons, daedra and more), while those with no match keep their classic sprite, as do flyers and swimmers with no matching Morrowind flyer or swimmer
Morrowind People: the Daedra Seducer keeps her disguise until she transforms
Morrowind People: ghosts and wraiths are Morrowind's ancestor ghost, seen through, vampires wear their race's vampire face, werewolves stand as Bloodmoon's wolf and orcs are Orcs
Morrowind People: bodies are drawn for the nearest people only within one budget for the whole frame, and everyone farther away or seen from the travel view keeps the classic sprite
Morrowind People: third-person Morrowind bodies, the player's included, are skinned on the graphics card instead of the CPU
Morrowind People: a new Morrowind People setting under Settings > Combat > With Morrowind data is Off, Near (the default, up to 24 bodies) or All (up to 48)

Travellers: new travellers set out from the towns: farmers leading a pack horse to market day, hunters heading into the wild, patrols of knights walking a round between a city and its region's towns, nobles travelling between courts with retainers and minstrels going to play another town's tavern
Travellers: bigger towns send out more pedlars, pilgrims and couriers

Travellers: parties at night stop at a roadside inn when one is close ahead and otherwise make camp with a fire, and parties meeting on the road greet each other once, warn each other of trouble behind and share a camp when they stop near each other
Travellers: roads a patrol has walked recently see half the trouble, and a patrol knight who sees a wanted criminal draws on them, even one the knight is on good terms with

Caravans: a merchant's caravan travels with a horse and wagon (two wagons from a great house's city) with its guards walking in front and behind, a noble's procession brings a baggage wagon, and pedlars and farmers lead a pack horse
Caravans: the wagons' wheels turn as they roll, at camp the wagons are parked around the fire with their horses unhitched, and a caravan's mark on the travel map is a wagon
Caravans: talking to a caravan's merchant, a farmer or a pedlar on the road allows buying and selling, each keeping a shop's stock and a limited purse for the trip and giving friends 10% off

Caravans: a merchant's caravan offers a guard contract from the day before it sets out until it arrives, paid by the day plus more for each foe beaten if the player stays within 300 m, unpaid if they fall behind over an hour, let the merchant die or rob or kill any of them, and offline the player can travel on with the caravan to its next stop

Caravans: beating every guard of a caravan makes it surrender, its goods and purse are the player's to take, and any survivor who reaches a town reports the theft, pickpocketing or murder as a crime in the region where it happened
Outlaws: each region has up to four named bands of outlaws with a hideout off a road between two of its towns, and a band holds up the parties too weak to fight it off and keeps what it took

Outlaws: a found hideout shows tents, a fire, the band and a chest of stolen goods, and killing every outlaw routs the band, with the dead staying down on return, the robbed people grateful, the region's towns talking about it and a new band moving in later
Outlaws: travellers warn about camps near the road they are on, and a band the player has heard of is marked on the travel map as a rumoured hideout, near it but never exactly on it

Adventuring Companies: adventurers travel together in named companies such as "The Lantern Company" and dive dungeons more often as a group, and pilgrims going the same way on the same day travel as a band, with each region keeping its own holy day for pilgrims setting out for its temple towns
Adventuring Companies: a company introduces itself by name, and the chronicle's People page lists the companies of the people the player knows
Adventuring Companies: a company works through a dungeon stop by stop and block by block, so they are wherever their route has brought them and fighting may be heard ahead before they are seen
Adventuring Companies: talking to a company lets the player have them join, lead on to their next stop or part ways, badly hurt members fall back and a beaten company heads for the exit

Adventuring Companies: offline, for a day after a company passes through, the monsters at the places they reached lie dead with their packs emptied and the treasure there picked over, while quest monsters and items and fixed monsters and treasure are never touched and the room's dungeon is unchanged online
Adventuring Companies: a rival company that is not friendly will not like the player taking treasure it was heading for

Town Buyers: a trader hired in a home open to the public sells to the town's people as well as players, who may buy a listed piece at the player's price every hour, more likely the lower the price against the piece's worth and never above 60% of its worth
Town Buyers: pieces bought at a shop counter online never sell to townspeople, who buy only what was found, looted or made

Town Buyers: a town's traders sell at most four pieces an hour between them and each seller at most two an hour and 20,000 gold a day, market tax and fees apply as for a sale to a player, quest items and keepsakes never sell this way and a crafted piece sells for no more than a found one
Town Buyers: the buyer is seen walking into the house a little later, some townspeople just come in to look, and the Vendor page shows who bought what, such as "Sold to Ada Lark of Wayrest"
Town News: news travels between towns: travellers bring what their home town knew when they set out and couriers bring news from one town further
Reputation: the player's reputation travels too, so strangers who have heard of their deeds, good or bad, may greet them by them, though hearsay alone never makes anyone a friend or an enemy

Prices: books and potion recipes no longer jump to a much higher price after passing between players online through a shared container or a shop's shelf in a room, which let them sell back for more than they cost

Weapon Techniques: Magic, Rare and Legendary weapons can drop with a technique, a special attack with its own key (by default the mouse's back side button, rebindable under Controls > Combat), found on Gauntlets for unarmed fighters, with a Tech button for touch corners on phones and d-pad placement on controllers

Weapon Techniques: bows can carry Volley (aim a circle and six arrows rain down on it) or Piercing Shot (one fast arrow passing through up to five foes), and the Dwarven Thunderlock can carry Piercing Shot
Weapon Techniques: long blades can carry Leap Strike (leap onto a foe up to 9 m away and hit everything around the landing) or Whirlwind (hit everything around the player)
Weapon Techniques: short blades can carry Shadowstep (dash behind a foe and strike) or Lunge (dash forward and hit everything passed)
Weapon Techniques: axes can carry Cleave (a wide sweep) or Headsman's Chop (hits harder the more wounded the foe is)
Weapon Techniques: blunt weapons can carry Ground Slam (hit everything around the player) or Skull Crack (one heavy, accurate blow)
Weapon Techniques: bare hands can carry Flying Kick (leap and strike) or Haymaker (one heavy, accurate punch)

Weapon Techniques: holding the key aims, with a blue ground marker showing where a Volley lands or a leap ends and turning red when out of reach, letting go fires, a quick tap fires at once where the player looks, and techniques that need no aiming go off on the press
Weapon Techniques: under a low ceiling a leap flies a lower arc, and if no arc fits the player gets "No room to leap."
Weapon Techniques: the technique key does nothing while a window is open, such as a conversation, the pack or a menu
Weapon Techniques: an unidentified piece's technique works but is called "Your technique" until identified
Weapon Techniques: every technique costs fatigue and has a cooldown, the Enhanced HUD shows a chip with the seconds left and the message line says when it is ready again
Weapon Techniques: damage still comes from Daggerfall's own formula, a technique multiplying a normal hit so a miss is still a miss, and the +N% on the item raises that multiplier

Weapon Techniques: techniques are disabled in duels and player-vs-player bouts and never hit another player, and a technique that hits all around only hits an ally or a peaceful creature where a normal swing would have
Weapon Techniques: techniques need the loot ladder, so with it off none drop and the key says why
Weapon Techniques: the Reforge shows what a technique does under its line, so it can be seen before reforging or honing

Item Card: a technique has its own section on the Enhanced item card, the way set pieces and sigils do, with a header of its glyph (three blue strike marks), its name and the roll (such as +23% [15-30]), what it does, and a footer with the key, hold-to-aim or press, the fatigue cost and the cooldown, and the shop's hover card shows the same
Item Card: the key shown is the one that actually works: the primary or secondary binding, or the controller button's name (A, Square, RB...) while playing on a controller
Item Card: the section is compact so item cards still fit without scrolling, dropping the hold-to-aim hint first and then the footer on a crowded card, while the Info box always shows everything

Item Card: the Info box shows the section in full with the word Technique over the name, how the roll raises the technique's own blow (such as 172% of a plain blow) and how to use the key, telling the player to bind Weapon technique in Controls if none is bound
Item Card: in a duel the section greys out and says why
Weapon Techniques: the HUD chip uses the same glyph as the card, says "unbound" if no key is bound, and hides during a duel like set-power chips
Item Card: the classic tooltip, the Reforge and the player-to-player trade window still show a technique as two lines
Weapon Techniques: Leap Strike and Flying Kick widen the view as the player leaves the ground, land with a hard dip and a thud, and spread a shock ring with thrown stone to the technique's reach
Weapon Techniques: Ground Slam raises the weapon and then slams the view down for the heaviest shake of all, with two shock rings racing across the floor with the most stone and sparks
Weapon Techniques: Whirlwind leans the view into the spin and flings sparks round a ring at its 3 m, carried the way the blade goes
Weapon Techniques: Cleave winds up the view leaning one way and lands leaning the other, with a fan of sparks following the arc

Weapon Techniques: Skull Crack, Headsman's Chop and Haymaker show a star of light and a spray of sparks where the blow lands, the Chop adding a ring under it and the Haymaker a ring standing in the air
Weapon Techniques: Shadowstep shows a quick high whisk and a ring of rising light where the player vanishes and a star where they strike
Weapon Techniques: Lunge leaves a trail of sparks down the lane the player ran
Weapon Techniques: Piercing Shot kicks the view up, flares and lays a tracer of sparks down the aim, stopping at the first thing in its way
Weapon Techniques: each of Volley's six arrows lands with a puff of stone exactly where and when it hits the ground, on slopes too, and a ring closes over the circle with the last one

Weapon Techniques: a Technique camera motion setting under Settings > Accessibility > Motion (Full, 75%, Half, Low or Off) scales the view's movement, the shake and the hands' dip, at Off the screen does not move while sparks and sounds stay, and sounds follow Sound Enhancements
Keybindings: polling a bound key no longer builds a list for every binding each time it is asked, so the game does less work every frame

Wagon: other players' horses and wagons more than 400 m away are no longer updated or drawn, so a town full of parked wagons no longer slows the game, and they reappear where they stand as the player nears

Wagon: off-screen wagons, carts, harnesses and tents are no longer drawn, covering the player's own and others' wagons, caravans and pack teams, the cart, camp tents and outlaw hideouts, while a just-off-screen shadow still falls into view
Loading: the game no longer fails to start with "boot failed: cannot access ... before initialization", which happened when starting near a port town or with the travel map's dungeon lists in play
Login: when many players sign in at once, such as right after an update, they wait in a short line instead of getting a "server" error, being told they are in line and keeping their place on retry

Performance: towns, woods and streets cost less to draw: still flats share large buffers instead of each patch of trees, plants and lamps carrying its own, cutting costly state switches almost in half with the same picture and about 14% less main-thread time in a night town

Performance: night-time towns make less garbage, since each lantern's shadow matrices are worked out in place and the shadow pass stopped creating temporary numbers for every lantern and tree pair, so there are fewer garbage-collector stutters
Performance: towns by a harbour are much cheaper, as moored ships no longer rebuild every part every frame, which cost up to 7 ms a frame near a port

Performance: busy servers stutter less: other players' name tags, footsteps and sprites make far less garbage, and their sprite art loads in idle time instead of all at once when turning toward a crowd
Performance: the first spell, the first fight and the first trip to the coast or sea no longer stall while their shaders compile, as those shaders are built in the background
Performance: the sky skips drawing stars during the day, when they cannot be seen
Performance: on laptops with two graphics cards the game asks for the faster one
Eye of the Beholder: in first person, looking up no longer shows the player's own body, which now follows the mod's visibility setting that by default casts the shadow but is never seen

DFO Grimoire: Main menu > Overhauls > UI has a fourth look, DFO Grimoire, which dresses everything Enhanced Plus does (hotbar, camps and tents, rest, maps, trading and every online panel) in GrimoireUI's parchment, wood, red-and-gold presses, glass vials and lettering
DFO Grimoire: the vitals are GrimoireUI's three vials, upright in the corner in Daggerfall's order or lying in a row under the hotbar

DFO Grimoire: the card has its own choices, each applied at once: Pages (cream page or tan scroll), Backdrop (the desk or the map), Vitals (upright or in a row) and Spellbook (the DFO book or GrimoireUI's own)
DFO Grimoire: the front door stands on a detailed desk as large as the screen allows, and every wooden board uses a soft desk wood
DFO Grimoire: rarity, set and sigil names are inked deeper on the page so they stay readable
HUD: the compass can be turned over in the HUD editor (Alt+U), with a new turn-over press beside the X
Main Menu: main menu clicks play the in-game click sound once the game data is loaded
Player Trade: letters of credit say what they are worth in the player-trade info box and hover
Wordmark: the Daggerfall Online logo is repaired, with the torn rows through "DAGGERFALL" and "The Elder Scrolls" mended and the clipped tops of its letters closed

Performance: towns and forests draw with far fewer graphics state switches, as the shared buffers for trees, plants and lamps grow to fit a large town and each kind of flat stays together, taking about 14% less main-thread time than before this change and about a quarter less than before the previous one

Notice Board: the Notice Board's trader directory, read by every player in a town, now looks only at the traders of its own region, so sign-ins, saves and everything else on the account service should stop failing under load
Online Players: other players far away are no longer drawn, where before everyone up to about 3 km away was animated and drawn every frame even when a pixel or two tall
Online Players: a new Draw distance setting on the Other players card chooses how far out other players are drawn: 150 m, 300 m (the default), 600 m or Everyone
Online Players: the party and the player being dueled always show at any distance
Online Players: at the default 300 m anyone close enough to hit with an arrow or a spell is still seen, while the 150 m option can hide a distant archer
Online Players: near the edge between two map areas each nearby player's position reaches the game mostly once instead of two to four times, cutting network traffic and CPU in busy towns
Online Players: other players move as smoothly as before
Wagon: the Small Cart's boards and stakes run square to its box, where they used to sit about 10 degrees off, most visibly with a horse in the shafts
Wagon: the Caravan's side windows are centred, one in the middle of each half of the side and midway between the trim lines, and still line up from inside
Wagon Parking: a wagon left parked on a road in a city, hamlet or village for 10 minutes is come for by a guard
Wagon Parking: a town holds four parked wagons, and when a fifth arrives the one parked longest is thrown out first, each player counting once per town so a second wagon of their own goes first
Wagon Parking: the guard walks up, lifts the wagon with its horses over their head and throws it out of town, tumbling through the air to land about 40 m past the town's edge
Wagon Parking: nothing is lost: the wagon keeps its cargo, paint and horse, and can be fetched or summoned, with summoning while the guard still carries it stopping the throw

Wagon Parking: the wagon usually lands on a side of town that keeps it in the same area, but in the biggest cities it lands just over the edge of the map square and appears once the player walks out to it
Wagon Parking: the player is told when the watch throws their wagon, or the next time they are back near it if they were not nearby
Wagon Parking: everyone nearby sees the throw, and a caravan the watch threw can still be visited where it lands
Wagon Parking: a player riding in the back of someone's wagon when the guard lifts it is set down first
Wagon Parking: a horse left on its own is never thrown, only wagons and carts, and a horse standing beside the wagon goes with it while one ridden off and left elsewhere stays put
Wagon Parking: offline the 10-minute road rule still applies, with the clock kept in the save so a wagon left on a road and loaded later is thrown as soon as the player is outdoors

Water Surface: from high ground the sea no longer fades into a pale band of fog ending in a hard square edge with a darker plane behind it, but runs on through the haze to the horizon in one piece, and the far sea reflects the sky the way the near water does
Water Surface: the far sea uses the same colour, light and sun glints as the water near the player so the two meet without a line
Water Surface: the far horizon that was already there shows the sea correctly at no extra cost and skips shading the parts hidden behind nearer ground

Home Votes: the door of another player's home offers Vote up and Vote down, becoming "Take back your vote" once voted, and on touch screens, the Classic interface or with World Tooltips off the door is clicked in Info mode to vote

Home Votes: each account has one vote per home, none on its own home, own guild's hall or a Knightly Order house, voting needs a username and password held for a week, up to 30 votes an hour can be cast and taking a vote back is always allowed

Home Votes: if a home's votes add up to less than zero other players see it as Daggerfall built it, with no placed decorations inside, nothing outside and the town's own paint, while a hired trader with goods stays open and the owner and a hall's guild members still see everything; nothing is deleted and the decorations return once the total is back to zero or above
Home Votes: once a home has votes its door shows the total, and the owner is told at the door or in the Info box when the decorations are hidden
Home Votes: a vote cast on a guild hall before joining that guild can still be taken back
Decorator: people placed with the decorator (the Vendors list), inside or in a yard, can no longer be resized, with Smaller and Bigger gone for them

Decorator: people placed earlier at another size now stand at their normal size, moving one sets it to normal, an enlarged one gives back half the price difference as shrinking any piece does and a shrunk one costs nothing to move
Thorns: thorns pay back at most 10 damage per blow, down from 25, which returned nearly two full sword swings every time a foe hit and let standing still in front of an Ancient Lich kill it
Thorns: thorns never deal the killing blow, wearing a foe down to its last point of health but leaving the player to finish it
Thorns: existing thorns gear keeps every line it rolled
Spite of the Spurned: Malacath's Bulwark four-piece bonus still returns its share of each blow but never takes a foe's last point of health
Troll's Blood: new Rare armour no longer rolls Cast When Held: Troll's Blood, which gave permanent regeneration on a piece that smiths can repair so it never wore out
Troll's Blood: pieces already owned keep it and stay valid online, and the Mages Guild item maker still sells it at Daggerfall's own price

Gems: graded gems (Chipped, Flawed, Flawless and Perfect stones, plus plain ones found the same way) drop about a third as often from bodies, dungeon piles and tavern or guild markers, a mid-level foe dropping one about once every 33 kills instead of 12 and the deepest dungeons and boss-level foes once every 20 sources instead of 7
Gems: a gem's grade still depends on where it is found, so a deep source still gives the Flawless and Perfect stones
Gems: the gems world bosses drop, the gems shops sell, Daggerfall's own gem drops and mined gems are unchanged

Performance: lamp shadows in towns at night take less work, a lamp reusing last frame's answer about which nearby plants and trees can cast into it when nothing near it has moved, with the shadows exactly the same
Performance: distant small flats are skipped before the game checks whether they are on screen, not after
Performance: the glow pass skips flats that have no glow before checking whether they are on screen

Performance: towns use less graphics memory, as the large shared buffers for trees, plants and lamps share one index buffer, saving about 6 MB per buffer and avoiding a short hitch when a new one opens

Enhanced Lighting: taverns, shops, homes and guild halls are no longer lit evenly wall to wall, since a building's own lamps burn at half their old strength and their light falls in warm pools with darker corners between
Enhanced Lighting: candles and other plain white lamps indoors burn with the same warm flame colour as the street lanterns
Enhanced Lighting: the player's eyes brighten a dim room less, so interiors stay moody instead of drifting toward grey
Tavern Cards: gold tables refused every buy-in with "You have too many stakes waiting to be settled" on every character, and buying in works again with no gold ever taken by the refusal
Tavern Cards: in the card table panel a refused stake shows as a warning, a stake being asked shows as a wait and the player's turn is highlighted
Tavern Cards: quick buttons set the stake, Min and Max for the buy-in and half pot and Pot for a raise, only moving the slider so the player still presses Deal me in or Raise
Tavern Cards: the stake slider shows its amount with its unit, gold or chips
Tavern Cards: a minus button in the panel's title hides the seats and the log so the table can be seen, while the message and the buttons stay
Tavern Cards: the log shows one line per event, with the newest line always visible
Keybindings: a key that is set but not confirmed says "Not saved yet - press Confirm." on its row
Keybindings: the top of the page counts the unsaved changes and highlights Confirm
Keybindings: the Confirm bar no longer hides behind the Settings search bar
Keybindings: on a phone the Confirm bar no longer covers the row being bound

Ship Helm: Recall, unstuck and other teleports from a ship's helm no longer leave the player stuck in the void, as the player leaves the helm the way fast travel does and a boat that can be packed goes back into the pack
Soul Trap: a soul-trapped Dragonling gives -5000 enchantment points as Soul Bound, where before only the rare quest Dragonling did and the ones met in the world gave 0
Online Mode: the update restarts the multiplayer server once, so everyone online is disconnected for a moment and reconnects on their own

Accounts: after a server update everyone online no longer reconnects in the same instant, each game waiting a moment, longer the more players are online, so the account service is not overwhelmed, while rejoining world chat takes no longer but the player's own area may take a few extra seconds to reappear
Online Mode: games in a crowded town send less, as a player with no enemies, camps, horses or boats around no longer repeats "nothing here" to everyone every two seconds
Accounts: asking for a sign-in token costs the account service fewer database reads
Accounts: the account, realm, heartbeat and profession reads a game keeps asking can be answered by read copies of the database, so they need not queue behind everyone's saves

Online Mode: after the next server update crowded towns cost the server far less, with other players' movements reaching the player in small bundles twenty times a second instead of one message per player per step and the world chat's list of who joined and left arriving once a second
Online Mode: after the next server update an area next to a duel, a Wrothgarian zone fight or a sea serpent fight says so, with the game sending it every step while it does

Live Chat: after the next server update world chat is no longer one server for everyone but is spread over sixteen by account so it holds many more at once, and the World tab still shows how many are online and lists them all while that is no more than 512
Live Chat: after the next server update typing /find <name> (or /who <name>) finds anyone online by name, and the Guild tab lists guildmates online wherever they are
Live Chat: after the next server update each region's chat is split four ways the same way, so a crowded start region lets everyone in faster, and the Region tab still lists everyone in the region

Room Copies: after the next server update a full town, building or dungeon no longer turns the player away but joins another copy of the same place (up to eight), a party in the open world joins its leader's copy, and a sea serpent, a raid, a circle-rite and the card tables stay with the main copy

World Bosses: after the next server update a world boss's court no longer turns players away when full, a newcomer joining a copy of the court to fight the same boss for the same rewards beside the players in that copy

Renown: the Renown earned reaches the server every few minutes instead of every minute to save the server a great deal of work, with the bar still showing what was earned at once (the faint part fills in when counted) and a level-up and the hour's limit still reported within the minute
Renown: once all the Renown an hour allows has been earned nothing more is collected until the next hour, since the server would not count it anyway
Caravans: with Morrowind models on, a road caravan's campfire is a fire again instead of a dead body
Wagon: the inventory's Cart slot shows the wagon the player actually drives, where it showed "Small Cart" for a player who still owned the old cart after buying a Caravan
Player Trade: a realm trade of an item looted in the last couple of minutes no longer fails with "The realm could not find the goods offered"
Slowfall: jumping works while Slowfall is active, at normal height with the descent at Slowfall's speed, though jumping in mid-air is still not possible
Gear Wear: Legendary items no longer lose condition when equipped, where the Aegis of Dawn lost about a third the first time it was put on, while other magic items still pay their usual cost

Yard: property lines are shared with neighbours, the ground between two houses split down the middle, so decorating in front of a neighbour's door is no longer possible and the player's own door step is theirs, though the marked edge on the ground has not changed shape yet

Dying: no single enemy blow can kill the player from full health but leaves them at 1 HP, and the next hit can still kill, with falls, spells, traps and world-boss attacks unchanged and a set's death saves (Unbroken, the Hour Turns) not used up on these blows

Come Sail Away: for owners of Come Sail Away boats, towns no longer lose frames for every boat placed wherever it is moored, where a fleet in a far-off port used to cost frames even deep inland, and other players' boats near the player cost less too
Come Sail Away: the sea's helm and broadside panels no longer do work every frame while the player is ashore

Tavern Cards: a tavern's card tables no longer stand in corridors, doorways or the mouth of an opening, fixing the table that shut off the back half of The Gold Dungeon in Menakat and the one across the way east in The Dancing Castle in Pilliweyn, and every other tavern laid out like them

Tavern Cards: a tavern with no floor for an out-of-the-way table has no card table (about one tavern in ten) and some keep only the green chips table, while almost every table that stays stands exactly where it stood

Snowfall: foes' ground telegraphs, like a revenant's blast circle, always draw on top of deep snow instead of being buried outdoors in winter, and the player's own technique marks are fixed the same way
Snowfall: deep snow can be turned off at Settings > Graphics > Sky, water & weather > Snowfall by demifiend000, which searching the settings for "deep snow" also finds

Player Trade: in a trade with another player each letter of credit shows its worth on its own row ("Worth 12,500 gold") across the pack, the offer and theirs, working on touch without hovering, and the item card shows it as Worth
Mining: copper, silver, platinum, moonstone, dwarven scrap, mithril, adamantium, ebony and orichalcum veins each have their own colour, while lead and lodestone keep their classic look
World Map: online, pointing at open ground on the world map shows a card of the ground's ore information
World Map: the card lists the ores the ground's veins can be
World Map: the card lists what the ground's dungeons' deep veins hold
World Map: the card lists the ground's kingdom's own ore (Daggerfall's Moonstone, Sentinel's Ebony, Wayrest's Mithril and so on)
World Map: the card says whether that ground is witnessed yet

Mining: Gold, Platinum, Mithril, Ebony and a kingdom's own ore only appear on ground that three different players, each on an account at least a week old, have gathered on, since the servers cannot check which land a player claims to stand on; the map card shows which ores are waiting on that for each place and the Mining page points to it
Sea Serpent: Sethrakul's waters stay open until it dives, so the 08:00 storm no longer locks ships out and latecomers and friends sailing out to help can still join
Sea Serpent: the serpent has a sixth less health so fights end sooner, with two ships at average gunnery now winning every time in about 8.5 minutes
Sea Serpent: one ship alone still cannot bring the serpent down
Sea Serpent: inside its waters a gale fills the sails from every direction, so there is no more beating upwind at half speed
Sea Serpent: a ship turns 1.5 times faster while in the serpent's waters
Sea Serpent: its blows throw a ship half as far and tear half as much canvas, so a ship is not pushed out of the fight and left unable to sail back
Sea Serpent: Sethrakul is much thicker, 1.6 times its old girth, so slow cannonballs fired with lag still land
Sea Serpent: players standing on someone else's ship can hurt the serpent with their own bows and attack spells
Sea Serpent: ships in the serpent's waters have a wide invisible buffer and bounce off each other instead of colliding and passing through
Sea Serpent: rewards no longer depend on being near the serpent when it dies
Sea Serpent: dealing a real part of the damage (several volleys that land) earns a hoard, and spending a quarter of the fight within range does too, where half was needed before
Sea Serpent: when the serpent falls, party members of any ship that dealt heavy damage also get a hoard as long as they came to the fight

Readied Spellcasting Hands: with a spell readied the casting hands are raised and ready on screen until the cast (jefetienne's Readied Spellcasting Hands 1.3 ported 1:1), self-only spells raising nothing since they cast at once, on by default and switchable under Features > Combat

Chat Window: the chat has a search bar above the player list (over the conversation on narrow screens) where part of a name, or # and a tag, shows every tab's lines from or about that player and filters the player list to match
Chat Window: typing /search <name> in the chat field searches and /search alone clears it, while /find and /who still look up who is online anywhere in the world
DFO Grimoire: text on the parchment is readable again, with the Social panel, letters, the guild page and typed-in fields in the page's ink
DFO Grimoire: the stray ruled lines are gone from the talk window, Professions and Master Skills
DFO Grimoire: enemy and boss health bars scale with the screen resolution, no longer drain or sit on a board, and stretch cleanly when lengthened in the HUD editor (Alt+U)
HUD: in the HUD editor (Alt+U) the length handle follows the pointer and resizing a piece no longer pushes it off the screen
DFO Grimoire: in the in-game book a setting's description opens as a scroll beside the book instead of covering the list, and the Controls header no longer hides the rows while scrolling
DFO Grimoire: in the decorations menu the selected tabs and filters can be seen
World Map: the world and town maps have their Find me button back, though it is still hidden on the dungeon's hand-drawn map
Hotbar: spamming the hotbar no longer makes the game stutter
Quest Journal: typing in the quest journal's note field works again on the classic and Grimoire UIs, opening as the game's standard text-entry box

Disenchanting: pressing a home's enchanting station asks for Daggerfall's item maker (Make Magic Items) or Disenchant, which opens the Stores page scrolled to the Enchanting Station section where a crafted piece comes apart into Arcane Essence
Alchemy Station: the alchemy station works the same way, offering Make Potions or Brew on the Stores page
Disenchanting: offline, both stations open Daggerfall's maker as before
Guild Tab: the Members page shows whether each member is online the way the Friends list does: a green dot while they are playing and "Online" or "Last online 3 h ago" under their rank
Guild Tab: a member counts as online while in the world (within ten minutes of their last check-in), and the time keeps updating while the page is open
Tutorials: the old tutorial is gone and new characters get a short welcome tour covering moving and climbing, using things, the HUD, and the menu and saving
Tutorials: any key a tutorial mentions is the key currently bound, named the way it appears on the keyboard

Tutorials: the first time the player reaches something new a short note explains it, with about 56 systems having one, from the inventory, spellbook, maps and the Overworld to shops, banks, guilds and card tables, horses and wagons, boats and sea battles, Dagon's Breach, the arena and the Abyss Dungeon, family, revenants and companions, gathering, professions and survival, and chat, parties, duels and the open zone
Tutorials: each note shows once and closes on a click or key press
Tutorials: notes will not close from a key already being held
Tutorials: notes wait until the pause menu and loading screens are gone
Tutorials: a Tutorials tab in the pause menu and a Tutorials button on the main menu hold all 68 notes in 13 sections
Tutorials: the notes can be searched and unread ones are marked
Tutorials: popups can be turned off, all shown again, or everything marked read

Online Players: other players no longer look like they float above the ground or sink into it, since their height was being rounded to the nearest metre on its way to the player and could be up to half a metre off
Online Players: in dungeons, towns and buildings other players no longer move in one-metre jumps
Online Mode: the update restarts the online server once, so everyone online is disconnected briefly and reconnects

Guild Tab: Members has a folded list, "What each rank may do", showing every rank's powers in the guild's own rank names, each rank on top of the one below, and what a rank may not do (Officers and the Guildmaster do not fill their own guild's writs or get paid by its contracts), and saying a Member and a Recruit hold the same powers
Guild Treasury: Treasury says which of the gold can buy a hall or a new name or tag: only gold the realm characters put in

Guild Treasury: the silver ledger says which way each line went, with a Tribute, upkeep or claim fee reading "paid ..." where it read "put in", and a line the guild made itself, such as a Sellsword hired or a Charter's upkeep, reading as the guild's

Guild Tab: Settings lists everything that still stands in the way of disbanding before pressing (gold, the hall, the vault, guild Stores, open writs or contracts, a Charter, a battle, and silver the account has no room to take), Disband and Leave for a lone guildmaster wait on it and say why, and opening Settings checks again
Guild Tab: Overview says where the rest of the guild is run: seats and sieges from a seat town's Notice Board and writs and contracts from the Work tab
Guild Tab: with no guild yet, the tab says in two lines what a guild is for
Silver: silver is called silver everywhere, including a siege's Honour, a struck Charter's refund and the daily reset that said "Marks"
Fealty: a vassal's 5% to its liege is its "fealty share", so "Tribute" means only what a guild pays at the seat it pledged
Heraldry: a guild's heraldry is called its "arms" everywhere, as on the Arms page
Arrows: a shot that misses stays in the wall, floor, tree or ground it hit and can be taken back like any other pile (the plaque reads "Arrow" and quick loot takes it in one press)
Arrows: up to 40 stay in one place, the oldest going first, and they are gone once the player leaves the area
Arrows: conjured arrows still vanish, and arrows shot in an arena bout are still refunded by the healers instead of sticking
Arrows: an arrow that hits an enemy survives half the time and can be looted from the body
Arrows: arrows no longer count toward a normal enemy's three-item drop limit, which was throwing them away first and is why bodies almost never gave arrows back
Arrows: using Twigs, a Pine Branch or a Wood Bundle from the inventory (Use mode) fletches 2, 4 or 10 arrows, online and offline
Shops: Weapon Smiths always keep 50-100 arrows on the counter, Armorers and General Stores 14-29 and Pawn Shops 7-14, better shops keeping more
Daggerfall Online: Daggerfall Online is now DFO Online, with a new logo on the intro, the main menu, the menu's masthead, the website and the desktop launcher
Desktop App: the website, desktop app, installer and home-screen app all carry the new name, the home-screen label reading DFO

Daggerfall Online: settings and menus say "the original game" or "classic" where they used to name it, for example "Off uses the classic weather", the leveling choice and classic start are titled Classic and the third view-distance step reads Classic (3)
Daggerfall Online: screenshots and saved loading shots are named dfo-... and exported saves are DFO-Online-Saves.zip
Desktop App: downloads are named DFO-Online-... from this update on, and an installed copy finds its update as usual whatever it was called when installed

Desktop App: on a Mac the new version installs as DFO Online beside the old Daggerfall Online app instead of replacing it, to be dragged to the Bin once DFO Online opens, with saves, settings and game folder staying where they are
Desktop App: on Windows a pinned taskbar or Start menu entry may need pinning again under the new name
Terms: the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy name DFO Online, with nothing else changed and no one asked to agree again
Tavern Cards: going all in and losing at an online Hold'em table no longer crashes the game, the hand that broke the player playing out on the table before they are stood up
Dungeon Map: with All pressed, the 3D dungeon map draws every ramp in full, where Daggerfall's standard ramps used to be cut off at the floor below
Raiding Parties: kills made after a raid's fight drifts past the edge of town count as long as the player is still on the town's map square
Raiding Parties: dying, fast travelling, Recall or /unstuck in the middle of a raid no longer stops raiders from coming when the player returns
Raiding Parties: the raid card on the map shows the town's real count against its real target (anywhere from 15 to 25), not only the player's own kills
Loot Window: the loot list on a body or pile scrolls, so the mouse wheel (or the pad) reaches every item, not only the first six, and the list shows how many items are above and below
Quests: people placed by a quest show their name when looked at, like everyone else in the room
Player Trade: when the realm refuses a trade because a character is under review it says whose character it is, the player's own with the reason or the other player's
Elite Gates: Elite Gates arrive, the Elite Breach and the Battlespire's torn halls
Spells: re-casting an effect already on the player or a target resets it to that cast's full duration instead of adding the new duration on top, and a shorter re-cast never cuts a longer one short

Spells: the reset applies to buffs and debuffs alike, covering Shield, Fortify, Regenerate, Levitate, Light, Detect, the resistances and the rest, Paralyze, Silence, Continuous Damage and Soul Trap, a party member's spells on the player and a torch's fire on a foe
Spells: re-casting Regenerate or a Continuous Damage effect on its last round still gives the full number of ticks a fresh cast would
Spells: buffs banked before the update keep their time and run out normally, and can be ended from the buff icons
Saves: with a window open, F11 (Quick Load) works only from the death screen, since loading from under the pack, a loot window or a sell counter could duplicate what that window was holding
Saves: any load closes every open window before the save is read, including windows left waiting behind the death screen

Shops: shops pay for a crafted Superior or Masterwork piece what they pay for the plain piece its recipe makes, since the quality's magic or rare lines are power not resale value, and the piece keeps them and its worth to other players
Shops: patrons follow the same rule for crafted pieces, while found magic and rare items are priced as before
Shops: the keyed shelf prices a sale exactly as the trade window does and no longer buys conjured (Create Item) pieces

Player Trade: a character whose trade is on hold can no longer move its crafted pieces through another character by listing, auctioning, filling a commission or disenchanting, and its Stores cannot go into a guild's Stores or fill a guild writ
Yard: other players' yard decorations no longer draw across the whole map, their small pictures (flowers, signs, crates) which had no distance limit now stopping where the models stop
Yard: tiny yard pieces stop drawing once they would be only a few pixels tall, so a busy street of furnished yards costs much less
Yard: a new option, Settings > Other players > Yard decorations, is Off, 75 m, 150 m or 300 m (the default, as before), with the player's own yard always shown
Yard: yard pieces still standing above the 4 m height limit (built before the limit existed) have been removed with no gold refunded
Accounts: a username can no longer be an email address, and a player who signed up with one still signs in with it but other players see a generated name instead of the address
Seat Tab: the board's Seat tab no longer gets stuck on "The standings did not load." once many guilds have pledged
Seats: the weekly Turning hands out Charters again, a guild that earned a seat last week being given it the first time anyone reads a seat after the update

Travellers: caravans and travellers keep to the right of the road, so parties that meet pass side by side instead of walking through each other's wagons, and two caravans heading the same way walk abreast
Caravans: a wagon follows its horse round a bend instead of swinging round all at once
Caravans: at a shared camp every caravan's wagons park round one fire without standing in each other, and each horse is tied alongside its cart
Caravans: in a roadside hold-up, fighters and bandits no longer stand inside the wagons and horses
Caravans: a roadside fight the player walks up to no longer ends by itself, killing the caravan's guards and counting as a win never fought
Caravans: a merchant whose caravan will meet trouble offers to hire the player, so the missing offer no longer gives that away
Dungeons: remains found in a dungeon are no longer laid again after saving and loading inside it
Townspeople: townsfolk walking into a shop are inside as soon as they reach the door
Townspeople: in town, people no longer stand inside one another in a three-person conversation
Seats: the weekly seat Turning can no longer swamp the servers, as only one request at a time settles the week and everyone else's seat board answers immediately
Seats: acting at a seat (pledge, Tribute, a lever) in the moment the week is turning gives "The week is turning at the seats. Try again in a moment." and is never applied to a half-turned week

Shipyards: port towns have a shipyard on their seaward edge with its back to the water, where the shipmaster sells every ship Come Sail Away builds, from the Rowboat to the Carrack and the Large Galley, and buys the player's ships back, in one window for everything done with a ship at a port

Shipyards: Ships for sale lists each hull's size, crew, guns and price, buying asks for confirmation, the Rowboat goes into the pack as parts and every other ship's deed goes into the Fleet with her laid up at that port, where Bring her here brings her round to the quay

Shipyards: Your fleet shows where each ship lies, what she is worth and what the shipmaster will pay, with options to bring her here, lay her up, rename or sell her, selling asking for confirmation and a big sale paid as a letter of credit if the coin would be too heavy
Shipyards: Shipwright and Refits cover repairs, provisions and the four refit lines for any ship of the player's at that port or laid up, and need Naval Combat on

Shipyards: the shipmaster will not buy a ship with cargo in her hold, anything in her cabin (in its chests or on its floor) or her crew ashore with the player, or a ship that came into the realm through customs, and when a ship is sold her cabin's furniture is sold too with half its value going to the bank, as with a house

Crew Halls: inside every shipyard the crewmaster has six named sailors looking for a berth each day, each with a class, a grade from Green to Veteran, a trade (First Mate, Bosun, Gunner, Carpenter, Lookout, Cook, Deckhand or a Bard) and a signing fee, and the player chooses which ship they join and at what post

Crew Halls: a ship comes with her whole crew, so on a full deck a recruit signs on in place of a chosen hand, a hire that adds men costs what the shipwright would charge if that is more than the fee, and hands can be paid off from the same page (naming who steps up if the crew still fills her deck, and never the last hand), with hiring and paying off needing Naval Combat on and not possible during a fight

Lighthouses: port towns have a lighthouse, a whitewashed stone tower with red bands, a gallery and a lantern room with the keeper's cottage beside it, whose lamp lights the harbour while the town's lanterns are lit (5 pm to 8 am) with two beams sweeping a full circle over the sea and town and seen in the same place by everyone online

Lighthouses: talking to the lightkeeper (or pressing the door) climbs up to the gallery on foot, not at a ship's helm and not with enemies about, with no way to fall or climb off the gallery and the hatch taking the player back down

Quays: every quay is overhauled with cross-braced piles, timbers under the decks, fender piles and iron ladders down into the water, cleats and coils of rope by the bollards, a cargo crane on each harbour's main quay and lamp posts along the long jetties

Shipyards: townsfolk can tell the player where to find the shipyard, crew hall, lighthouse and docks, the shipyard and lighthouse are marked on the town map, and on the Overworld the shipyard, lighthouse and docks show as an anchor, a tower and a bollard
Shops: General Stores and Pawn Shops no longer sell or buy ship deeds and parts, since ships are bought and sold at the shipyards

Tutorials: the tutorial's Sailing page sends the player to the shipyards, Shipwrights is now Shipyards (the shipmaster, the crew hall and the shipwright), there is a new Lighthouses page, and the empty Fleet page and Come Sail Away's setting point to the shipyards too
Shipyards: a ship sold while being placed could be placed and sold again
Shipyards: a double click could buy two ships
Crew Halls: paying off a hand could put a stranger on deck, and hiring could raise a wreck back afloat
Crew Halls: hiring and paying off could push a ship's morale past its limit
Crew Halls: the crew page did not show which hands were ashore with the player
Lighthouses: climbing or jumping on the lighthouse gallery could take the player over the railing
Lighthouses: coming down the lighthouse stair could leave the player stuck in the door's step
Lighthouses: the lighthouse lamp was blocked by its own glass and barely lit anything with Enhanced Lighting
Lighthouses: the lighthouse sometimes stood right beside the shipyard instead of along the shore
Harbours: a lake behind a port town could be taken for the sea
Shipyards: selling a ship lost whatever lay on her cabin floor
Shipyards: roofs, beams and posts on the shipyard and the lighthouse no longer flicker and props no longer poke through each other
Harbours: ports, lighthouses and quays run lighter, the lighthouse lights costing nothing per frame, the port's textures loading over a few frames and the quays' hidden timbers left out of collision
Crew Roles: every hand earns rank from the fights and boardings they have been through: Green, Seasoned, Veteran, Old Salt

Crew Roles: the six posts aboard each do more the longer their holder has served: the Gunner speeds the reload, the Carpenter the mending, the Lookout lets the player see further, the Cook keeps spirits up, the Bosun adds way under sail and the First Mate brings extra hands over the rail (never more than the crew has men for)
Crew Roles: a companion who sails with the player works his post while the player is at the helm
Crew Roles: a new hand takes whichever post is emptiest, so a fallen Cook is replaced before a third Bosun, and posts can still be reassigned on the Fleet page
Captain Tab: a Captain tab in Holdings keeps a log of leagues sailed, ships sunk, taken and beaten off, contracts done, the best prize and the plunder hauled

Captain Standing: the player builds standing with each crown from Unsworn to Admiral, with perks in that crown's harbours: a shipwright discount, better-paid and more contracts, a letter of marque for sale (Privateer), the Admiralty's carrack for sale and seasoned hires (Commodore) and the navy always coming to aid against pirates (Admiral), none of them where notoriety runs too high
Boarding: beating off a pirate boarding now pays, the pirate being beaten then, so taking or sinking her afterwards is logged but not paid again
Captain Standing: a letter of marque makes a rival crown's merchantmen and navy lawful prize in the player's crown's eyes, though the rival still calls it piracy
Deep Waters: far from every port pirates are more common, bolder and bigger and every hold and floating cask is richer, and the helm plate says when the player is in the deep
Spyglass: ship names no longer float over every sail: a ship not yet identified is just her hull, such as "a sloop" or "a two-master", and her card says nothing else, no colours and no damage
Spyglass: a ship's colours are learned by sailing close, from the Lookout's call, when her guns turn on the player, or through the spyglass

Spyglass: pressing K aboard raises the glass and the mouse wheel zooms (x2, x4, x8), holding it on a ship reads her name and colours and up close shows her guns, crew, damage and cargo, but it cannot see ships behind land or dark ships far off at night

Spyglass: some wary pirates sail under false colours, passing for a merchantman of their own size with a trader's name, which the glass sees through, and they run up the black flag when they come for the player

Spyglass: on a controller the d-pad press given the Spyglass works at the helm too and the right stick's click zooms while the glass is up, and on a touch screen the Glass button sits at the helm and as a corner-button choice with its own Magnify and Lower buttons

Harbourmaster: every port's shipwright window has a Harbourmaster tab with the day's contracts while the ship lies at that port's quay: bounties on a named pirate, hunts in the crown's waters, cargo to carry to another port, a wreck's casks to raise and Admiralty surveys of ships through the spyglass

Harbourmaster: contracts pay by level and rank and run to a deadline, finishing one raises standing with the crown while failing or giving one up lowers it, three can be held at a time and the Captain tab lists them, each kill or survey counting toward one contract

Harbourmaster: a bounty's pirate waits in the waters named on the contract and the bounty is void with no loss of standing if someone else sinks her first, and a wreck's casks float up when the player reaches its mark

Exchange: an Exchange tab buys and sells eight goods of the Bay (wine, grain, wool, iron, spices, silk, silver and ivory), each crown's ports making some goods cheaply and paying well for others, with a twist of its own at every port, prices drifting day to day and each port dealing in only so much of a good each day
Exchange: goods load into and out of the hold of the ship at the quay, a full hold slows her, and the exchange says how much more she can carry and will not sell her so much she cannot move
Shops: shops do not buy the exchange's goods, which are sold at an exchange

Treasure Charts: pirates sunk or taken sometimes carry a treasure chart, more often in the deep waters and most flagships, which is read from the inventory to mark its cache so that sailing to the spot raises gold and a strongbox's worth of loot beside the ship, a cache once raised staying raised

Etheric Sea: sailing far out on the open Abecean, west of the Bay's mouth and well away from land, asks whether to sail on into the open sea, and three days later the ship comes out off Veilhaven, the first port past the Veil, with her crew and hold, with sailing back into the Veil at the eastern edge asking the way home and a warning if an enemy is close or another player is aboard

Etheric Sea: past the Veil lies an endless sea of isles, the same for every player: port isles have a town and a freeport quay, ruins a dungeon to delve, wild isles exotic goods and bare rocks are just rocks

Etheric Sea: the farther west one sails, through the Shallows, the Reaches, the Deep Aether and the Abyss, the deadlier the corsairs and the richer every hold, with ruins in the Deep Aether and the Abyss being Elite dungeons

Etheric Sea: no crown's law reaches past the Veil, so there is no navy to call on and nothing sunk there counts as a crime, corsairs and the isles' traders sail under the sea's own names and a corsair's papers sometimes chart her waters

Etheric Sea: ether-amber, starglass and voidsilk are made on the isles and wanted in every port of the Bay, the isles pay well for the Bay's goods, and sailing close to a wild isle floats casks of its good out alongside the ship, its strand filling again seven days after it is first gathered

Etheric Sea: six legendary ships haunt the depths, Sorrow's Wake, The Drowned Queen, Ninefold Hunger, The Lantern-Eater, The Pale Regent and The Starless, each with her own terror and a purse on her head, a freeport's harbourmaster telling where each was last seen, and sinking one earning her purse and a name with every crown before the sea raises her again a month later

Etheric Sea: past the Veil the travel map key opens a chart of the isles sighted, the depths, the Veil and the haunts of the legends heard of, which pans by dragging and zooms with the wheel, a pinch or the chart's own buttons, names an isle on pointing or tapping, charts isles as they are sighted and is sold for a freeport's waters by that freeport

Etheric Sea: the Veil holds the Bay's magic back, so Recall, guild teleports, portal stones and a party's travel to its leader do not cross it, the Fleet cannot summon or send a ship across, and falling past the Veil wakes the player at the nearest port isle
Etheric Sea: the light past the Veil is cold and violet
Etheric Sea: the crossing out is part of the enhanced game and online play, while the classic game keeps Daggerfall's own sea, though a captain already past the Veil can always sail home
Gathering: a herb patch, vein, boulder or tree goes the moment the player finishes working it instead of waiting for the server to answer, and comes back if the server refuses the harvest
Gathering: goods, XP and rank-ups arrive faster after each harvest
Market: the market loads noticeably faster, especially when switching views and after buying
Market: a view opened in the last minute shows straight away without a "Reading the market..." flash
